definition_zh: 放弃；抛弃；遗弃；放任；纵情
definition_en: to leave someone or something behind for good, or to give up an aim
core_image: 一串钥匙留在桌上，人转身出门，门在身后合上
scene: 雨夜，他把车停在路边，锁上门，沿着公路往下一个镇走。He decided to abandon the car and walk to the next town.
sceneCN: 这里 abandon 是「丢下、抛弃」（第 3 个义项：把车这类东西弃在一边）；句意是他决定丢下车子，步行去下一个镇。桌上那串钥匙，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 动词：放弃；抛弃；遗弃；放任
名词（书面）：放纵、尽情（多用于 with abandon）

derivatives.zh: 加 -ment 构成，义为「放弃、遗弃」
义为「被遗弃的；放纵的」
义为「遗弃者」

senses.title: To give up an aim
senses.titleCN: 放弃目标
senses.definition: stops trying to do or achieve something
senses.definitionCN: 停止尝试做某事或达成某个目标
senses.example: They had to abandon the climb before dark.
senses.exampleCN: 他们不得不在天黑前放弃登顶。
senses.why: The oldest French sense is to hand something over, and giving up a plan is handing it away.
senses.whyCN: 古法语最古老的意思是「交出去」，放弃计划就是把计划交出去。

senses.title: To leave someone behind
senses.titleCN: 抛弃某人
senses.definition: leaves a person without help or support
senses.definitionCN: 丢下某人，不再给予帮助或支持
senses.example: He would never abandon a friend in trouble.
senses.exampleCN: 他绝不会抛弃陷入困境的朋友。
senses.why: To surrender control of a person is to stop standing by them.
senses.whyCN: 把一个人交出去不管，就是不再站在他身边。

senses.title: To desert a place or thing
senses.titleCN: 遗弃某地或某物
senses.definition: leaves a building, town or vehicle and does not return
senses.definitionCN: 离开房屋、城镇或车辆且不再回来
senses.example: The villagers abandon their homes when the river rises.
senses.exampleCN: 河水上涨时，村民会弃家而走。
senses.why: A place handed over to itself stands empty, so the verb covers deserted houses and cars as well.
senses.whyCN: 被交还给自己的地方就空了下来，动词因此也涵盖弃屋与弃车。

senses.title: To give up a claim
senses.titleCN: 放弃权利或主张
senses.definition: formally gives up a right, claim or plan
senses.definitionCN: 正式放弃某项权利、主张或计划
senses.example: The company agreed to abandon the lawsuit.
senses.exampleCN: 公司同意放弃这场诉讼。
senses.why: Legal surrender is the literal old sense, still visible in claims and lawsuits.
senses.whyCN: 法律上的让与正是古老的直义，在权利主张与诉讼里仍看得见。

senses.title: To let oneself go
senses.titleCN: 放纵自己
senses.definition: in abandon oneself to, gives way completely to a feeling
senses.definitionCN: 在「abandon oneself to」中完全沉入某种情感
senses.example: She abandoned herself to grief for a week.
senses.exampleCN: 她放任自己悲伤了一个星期。
senses.why: Giving up control of oneself produces the reflexive pattern and the noun abandon.
senses.whyCN: 放弃对自己的控制，便生出反身句型和名词 abandon。

senses.title: Complete lack of restraint
senses.titleCN: 放纵、尽情
senses.definition: in the phrase with abandon, acts freely and without shyness
senses.definitionCN: 在「with abandon」中自由自在、毫不拘束地行动
senses.example: The children danced with abandon in the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们在雨中尽情跳舞。
senses.why: A person who has surrendered caution moves without holding back, and the noun names that freedom.
senses.whyCN: 放下了谨慎的人不再收着，名词便指这种自由。

intro.en: The word came into English from French, where it meant to put something under someone else's control.
intro.cn: 这个词经法语进入英语，原意是「把某物交到别人掌控之下」。

items.en: a bandon meant at one's disposal or under one's control.
items.cn: a bandon 意为「听凭处置、在他人掌控之下」。

items.en: abandoner meant to give something over to another's power.
items.cn: abandoner 意为把某物交给他人支配。

items.en: abandonen entered English with the sense of handing over or surrendering.
items.cn: abandonen 进入英语时意为交出、让与。

items.en: the sense shifted from surrendering to leaving something behind.
items.cn: 词义从「让与」转为「丢下不管」。

items.en: the noun with abandon names a careless freedom.
items.cn: 名词搭配「with abandon」指一种无所拘束的自由。

note.en: The look-alike group is the abandon family; the near-meaning group is other verbs of leaving.
note.cn: 形近组是 abandon 词族；近义组是别的表示「离开、舍弃」的动词。

entries.definition: The act of leaving something for good.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「放弃、遗弃」。

entries.definition: Left empty or without care.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「被遗弃的、放任的」。

entries.definition: A person who gives someone up.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「遗弃者」。

entries.definition: More than enough; a different word with a similar shape.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「丰富的」，形似而不同源。

entries.definition: To leave a person or post without help.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「遗弃、擅离」。

entries.definition: To give up or leave for good, mostly in literary use.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「抛弃、弃绝」，多见于书面。

entries.definition: To stop doing or leave a place.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「停止、离开」。

entries.definition: To give up a right or possession, formally.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「放弃（权利、所有物）」，较正式。

normalIntro.en: These hints follow the French phrase a bandon and the family endings.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条贴着法语短语 a bandon 与整组词尾。

normal.en: a bandon meant under another's control, not free.
normal.cn: a bandon 意为「在他人掌控下」，并不自由。

normal.en: To abandon was first to hand something over.
normal.cn: abandon 最初就是「把东西交出去」。

normal.en: The -ment ending turns the act into a noun.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ment 把这个动作变成名词。

normal.en: 「abandon ship」 is the fixed call for leaving a sinking vessel.
normal.cn: 「abandon ship」是弃掉沉船的固定呼号。

normal.en: 「with abandon」 drops the object and names the mood.
normal.cn: 「with abandon」不带宾语，直接指那种心境。

abstract.en: See a key left on a table and a door closing.
abstract.cn: 想象一串钥匙留在桌上，门关上了。

abstract.en: Picture a car by the road with its lights still on.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆车停在路边，车灯还亮着。

abstract.en: Think of a kite let go and drifting away.
abstract.cn: 想象风筝脱手，越飘越远。

examples.en: They had to abandon the plan when the money ran out.
examples.cn: 钱用完之后，他们不得不放弃这个计划。

examples.en: The crew abandoned the ship before dawn.
examples.cn: 船员在黎明前弃船。

examples.en: She sang with abandon at the end of the concert.
examples.cn: 音乐会结尾时她尽情歌唱。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿班登」——阿班把行李一放，说了声不干了，转身就走。

root: 古法语 a bandon（听凭处置）到 abandoner（交出、放弃），本义「把事物交出去」，后引申为抛弃、放弃。

sensesIntro.en: Handing something over becomes giving it up, leaving people and places, and finally a carefree mood.
sensesIntro.cn: 把东西交出去，先是放弃，继而抛弃人与地方，最后成了一种无所拘束的心境。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a key left behind and a door closing.
core.cn: 核心意象：钥匙被留下，门被关上。

branches.en: the plan or aim given up
branches.cn: 被放弃的计划或目标

branches.en: people and places left behind
branches.cn: 被抛下的人与地方

branches.en: rights and claims dropped
branches.cn: 被舍弃的权利与主张

branches.en: restraint given up, hence freedom
branches.cn: 放弃约束，因而自由

branches.en: CONTRAST: keep is the same hand still holding on
branches.cn: 对照线：keep 是同一只手仍握着不放

intro.en: A French phrase turned verb, with the common endings that built its family.
intro.cn: 一个法语短语变成的动词，加上造出整族词的常见词尾。

latinIntro.en: The root is French a bandon; the Latin-style suffix -ment later names the act.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是法语的 a bandon；后来用带拉丁色彩的后缀 -ment 命名这个动作。

items.exampleCN: 它是军事语境里的近义词。

definition_zh: 能力；才能；本领
definition_en: the power or skill to do something
core_image: 一个人踮脚把高处的罐子稳稳取下来，旁边的人够不着
scene: 面试官翻着简历，问的不是学历，而是你能做什么。She has the ability to explain difficult ideas in simple words.
sceneCN: 这里 ability 是「能力」（第 1 个义项：做事的力量或本领）；句意是她有能力把复杂的想法用简单的话讲清。那个踮脚取罐子的人，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 名词：能力、才能（可数、不可数皆可）

collocations.phrase: to the best of one's ability

derivatives.zh: 去掉名词词尾得到的形容词，义为「有能力的」
由 en- + able 构成，义为「使能够」
由 dis- + able 构成，义为「使失去能力」
加否定前缀 in- 构成，义为「无能力」

senses.title: The power to do something
senses.titleCN: 做事的能力
senses.definition: the fact of being able to do something
senses.definitionCN: 能够做某事这一事实
senses.example: She has the ability to explain difficult ideas in simple words.
senses.exampleCN: 她有能力把复杂的想法用简单的话讲清。
senses.why: The -ity ending turns able into a name for the quality itself, so power becomes a noun.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -ity 把 able 变成这种性质本身的名称，力量因此成了名词。

senses.title: A learned or natural skill
senses.titleCN: 才能、本领
senses.definition: a skill, especially one that is natural or well trained
senses.definitionCN: 某种技能，尤指天生的或训练有素的
senses.example: His musical ability was obvious by the age of five.
senses.exampleCN: 他五岁时音乐才能就已很明显。
senses.why: A single talent can be counted, which is why the noun takes a plural.
senses.whyCN: 一项才能可以被计数，所以这个名词有复数。

senses.title: In the set phrase
senses.titleCN: 在固定短语中
senses.definition: in to the best of one's ability, with as much effort as one can give
senses.definitionCN: 在「to the best of one's ability」中，指竭尽自己所能
senses.example: I will finish the report to the best of my ability.
senses.exampleCN: 我会尽我所能完成这份报告。
senses.why: The phrase measures effort rather than talent: a person gives what power they have.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语衡量的是努力而非天赋：人把自己有的力量都拿出来。

intro.en: Ability is the Latin noun for being able, built on habilis, which also gives able.
intro.cn: ability 是拉丁语中表示「能」的名词，建于 habilis 之上，able 也出自这个词。

items.en: habilis meant easy to handle, and so fit or capable.
items.cn: habilis 意为「好使唤的」，因而指合适、有能力。

items.en: habilitas named the quality of being fit for a task.
items.cn: habilitas 指胜任某项任务的性质。

items.en: French shortened the word to ablete, the power to act.
items.cn: 法语把词缩短成 ablete，指行动的力量。

items.en: English took it as abilite, meaning power or skill.
items.cn: 英语借入为 abilite，意为力量或技能。

items.en: modern spelling fixed as ability, and it now covers skill as well as power.
items.cn: 现代拼写固定为 ability，如今既指力量也指技能。

note.en: The look-alike group is the able family; the near-meaning group holds other words for talent.
note.cn: 形近组是 able 词族；近义组收其他表示「才能」的词。

entries.definition: Having the power or skill to do something.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有能力的」。

entries.definition: The lack of power or skill.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「无能力」。

entries.definition: To give someone the power to act.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使能够」。

entries.definition: Having a condition that limits activity.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有残疾的」。

entries.definition: The power to do a particular kind of work.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「能力、性能」，多指特定任务。

entries.definition: A practised ability, learned by training.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「技能」，靠训练获得。

entries.definition: A natural ability, usually in art or sport.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「天赋」，多指艺术或运动。

entries.definition: The amount something can hold, or take in.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「容量、承受力」。

normalIntro.en: The hints use the able spine and the -ity ending that turns an adjective into a noun.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子利用 able 这个词干，以及把形容词变名词的 -ity 词尾。

normal.en: Ability is able plus -ity: the adjective's quality turned into a noun.
normal.cn: ability 是 able 加 -ity：形容词的性质变成名词。

normal.en: The pair able and ability differ only in word class, not in meaning.
normal.cn: able 与 ability 只差词性，意义不变。

normal.en: Add en- and you enable someone; add in- and you name the lack.
normal.cn: 加 en- 就成为「使能够」，加 in- 就指这种能力的缺失。

normal.en: 「to the best of one's ability」 measures effort, not talent.
normal.cn: 「to the best of one's ability」衡量的是努力，不是天赋。

normal.en: The Latin root habilis meant handy, so ability began as being easy to use.
normal.cn: 拉丁词根 habilis 意为「顺手好使」，所以 ability 起初是「好用」。

abstract.en: A hand reaching a high shelf without help is the whole noun.
abstract.cn: 一只手无需帮忙就够到高架子，就是这个名词的全部。

abstract.en: Power that has been trained becomes countable and takes a plural.
abstract.cn: 经过训练的力量变得可数，于是有了复数。

abstract.en: Every hire is a bet on an ability no one can see yet.
abstract.cn: 每一次录用都是对一项还看不见的能力下注。

examples.en: The job calls for the ability to work under pressure.
examples.cn: 这份工作要求能在压力下工作的能力。

examples.en: She showed great ability in mathematics at school.
examples.cn: 她上学时在数学上表现出很强的能力。

examples.en: He fixed the radio to the best of his ability.
examples.cn: 他尽自己所能把收音机修好了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿比勒提」——阿比勒一伸手就提到罐子，这叫能力。

root: 拉丁语 habilis（顺手好使、有能力）到 habilitas（能力），经古法语 ablete 成为英语 ability；同族词有 able、enable、inability。

sensesIntro.en: Ability names the power to act first, then a countable talent, and finally a phrase for effort.
sensesIntro.cn: ability 先指行动的力量，再指可数的才能，最后成了一个表努力的短语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand reaching a high shelf without help.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手不靠帮忙就够到高架子。

branches.en: POWER LINE: the bare fact of being able.
branches.cn: 力量线：能做事这一事实本身。

branches.en: SKILL LINE: one trained talent, countable.
branches.cn: 技能线：一项经过训练的才能，可数。

branches.en: EFFORT LINE: the set phrase measures how much one gives.
branches.cn: 努力线：固定短语衡量的是投入多少。

branches.en: CONTRAST: inability is the same shelf out of reach.
branches.cn: 对照线：inability 是同一个架子却够不到。

branches.en: RELATED: talent is the same power before training.
branches.cn: 关联线：talent 是训练之前的那种力量。

intro.en: The adjective able plus the noun ending -ity, with two prefixes that build opposites.
intro.cn: 形容词 able 加名词词尾 -ity，另有两个造出反义与使动的前缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin habilis, from habere to hold, is the ultimate root; -ity comes from Latin -itas.
latinIntro.cn: 最终词根是拉丁语 habilis（源自 habere「持有」）；-ity 来自拉丁语 -itas。

definition_zh: 有能力的；能够的；能干的
definition_en: having the power, skill or chance to do something
core_image: 一个人单手把沉重的箱子提起来，另一只手还空着
scene: 搬家那天，朋友看了一眼那台旧冰箱，说这种事得找两个人才行。She was able to finish the work before noon.
sceneCN: 这里 able 是「能够」（第 1 个义项：具备做某事的力量或条件）；句意是她能在中午前完成工作。那个单手提起箱子的人，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 形容词：有能力的、能够的；能干的、有才干的

derivatives.zh: 加 -ity 构成，义为「能力、才能」
加 -ly 构成，义为「能干地、出色地」
由 en- + able 构成，义为「使能够」
加否定前缀 un- 构成，义为「不能的」

senses.title: Having the power or chance
senses.titleCN: 能够、有条件
senses.definition: has the power, means or opportunity to do something
senses.definitionCN: 具备做某事的力量、手段或机会
senses.example: She was able to finish the work before noon.
senses.exampleCN: 她能在中午前完成工作。
senses.why: The Latin root names being fit for a task, and English keeps that fitness as power to act.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根指「胜任某事」，英语把这种胜任保留为行动的力量。

senses.title: Skilled and capable
senses.titleCN: 能干的、有本事的
senses.definition: used before a noun to praise skill
senses.definitionCN: 置于名词前，称赞某人本领高
senses.example: He is an able lawyer and a patient listener.
senses.exampleCN: 他是一位能干的律师，也是个耐心的倾听者。
senses.why: Placed before a noun, the same fitness becomes a compliment about a person.
senses.whyCN: 放在名词前，同样的「胜任」就变成对人的称许。

senses.title: In the fixed frame
senses.titleCN: 在固定结构中
senses.definition: in be able to, the usual way to say can in writing
senses.definitionCN: 在「be able to」中，是书面语里表达 can 的常用方式
senses.example: They were able to reach the village before the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 他们赶在暴风雨前到达了村子。
senses.why: Able needs a linking verb, so be able to fills the slot that can holds by itself.
senses.whyCN: able 需要一个系动词，于是「be able to」占住了 can 单独占据的位置。

intro.en: Able came from Latin through French, always keeping the sense of being fit for use.
intro.cn: able 经法语来自拉丁语，始终保留「适合使用」的意思。

items.en: habilis meant easy to handle, hence suitable and capable.
items.cn: habilis 意为「好使唤的」，因而指合适、能干。

items.en: French passed the word on as able with the same sense.
items.cn: 法语以 able 的形式传下来，意思未变。

items.en: English used able for being fit or suited to something.
items.cn: 中古英语用 able 表示适合、胜任某事。

items.en: the narrowed sense of having power to act became standard.
items.cn: 「有力量行动」这一收窄的义项成为标准用法。

items.en: the frame be able to spread as the written partner of can.
items.cn: 「be able to」这一结构普及，成为 can 的书面搭档。

note.en: The look-alike group is the able family; the near-meaning group holds other words for being capable.
note.cn: 形近组是 able 词族；近义组收其他表示「有能力」的词。

entries.definition: In a skilled, capable way.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「能干地」。

entries.definition: The noun for the power to act.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「能力」。

entries.definition: Not having the power to do it.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不能的」。

entries.definition: To give the power to do it.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使能够」。

entries.definition: Having the skill for a particular job.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有能力的」，多接 of。

entries.definition: Good enough to do the work properly.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「胜任的」，强调够格。

entries.definition: Trained and practised in a craft.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「熟练的」。

entries.definition: Suitable or healthy enough for a task.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「适合的、健康的」。

normalIntro.en: The hooks lean on the Latin root habilis and the frames that able lives in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子依靠拉丁词根 habilis 和 able 常处的句式。

normal.en: The root habilis meant handy, and an able person is handy for any task.
normal.cn: 词根 habilis 意为顺手好使，能干的做事都得手。

normal.en: Able never stands alone as a verb: it needs be able to.
normal.cn: able 不能单独作谓语，要靠「be able to」。

normal.en: Add -ity for the noun, add un- for the opposite.
normal.cn: 加 -ity 成名词，加 un- 成反义。

normal.en: Before a noun it turns praise: an able lawyer, an able student.
normal.cn: 放在名词前便成褒扬：an able lawyer、an able student。

normal.en: Ably is the adverb, and it hides inside words like comfortably.
normal.cn: ably 是副词，也藏在 comfortably 这样的词里。

abstract.en: Able is a door being open rather than a skill being listed.
abstract.cn: able 说的是一扇门开着，而不是一份技能清单。

abstract.en: Lifting a heavy box alone is the plainest picture of the word.
abstract.cn: 一个人提起重箱，是这个词最朴素的画面。

abstract.en: Every able hides a task it is fit for.
abstract.cn: 每个 able 背后都藏着一件它胜任的事。

examples.en: She was able to finish the work before noon.
examples.cn: 她能在中午前完成工作。

examples.en: He is an able lawyer and a patient listener.
examples.cn: 他是一位能干的律师，也是个耐心的倾听者。

examples.en: We were not able to reach the village before the storm.
examples.cn: 我们没能赶在暴风雨前到达村子。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「诶，宝」——诶，宝刀在手，什么都干得了，这就是 able。

root: 拉丁语 habilis（顺手好使、胜任）经古法语 able 进入英语；同族词有 ability、ably、enable、unable。

sensesIntro.en: Able first means having the power to act, then praises skill, and finally lives in the frame be able to.
sensesIntro.cn: able 先指有力量行动，继而用于称许本领，最后常驻于「be able to」这一结构。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one hand lifting a heavy box while the other stays free.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手提起重箱，另一只手仍空着。

branches.en: POWER LINE: having means or chance to act.
branches.cn: 力量线：具备行动的手段或机会。

branches.en: PRAISE LINE: placed before a noun, it compliments skill.
branches.cn: 称许线：置于名词前称赞本领。

branches.en: FRAME LINE: be able to does the work of can.
branches.cn: 结构线：「be able to」承担 can 的职责。

branches.en: CONTRAST: unable is the same box that will not move.
branches.cn: 对照线：unable 是同一个箱子却搬不动。

branches.en: RELATED: ability is this fitness turned into a noun.
branches.cn: 关联线：ability 是这种胜任变成的名词。

intro.en: A Latin adjective of fitness, with prefixes and suffixes that build the whole family.
intro.cn: 一个表「胜任」的拉丁形容词，加上造出整族词的前后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin habilis comes from habere, to hold; Latin -ibilis was the ending for can be done.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 habilis 出自 habere（持有）；拉丁语 -ibilis 是表「可被……的」词尾。

definition_zh: 在船（车、飞机）上；上船（车、飞机）
definition_en: on or onto a ship, train, plane or other vehicle
core_image: 舷梯放下来，人抬脚跨过船沿，站到甲板上
scene: 客轮离岸还有三分钟，检票员站在跳板边，一遍遍喊着请尽快上船。All passengers must be aboard before the ferry leaves.
sceneCN: 这里 aboard 是「在船上」（第 1 个义项：处于车船飞机之上）；句意为渡轮开动前所有乘客必须上船。那架放下的舷梯，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 介词：在……上、上……（船、车、飞机）
副词：在船上、上车、登机

derivatives.zh: 去掉前缀 a- 的词根，义为「木板；上船、登机」
同义短语，义为「在船上、在机上」
正式的固定说法，义为「在船上」

senses.title: On a vehicle
senses.titleCN: 在船、车、飞机上
senses.definition: on a ship, train or plane, as a passenger or crew
senses.definitionCN: 作为乘客或船员处在船、火车或飞机上
senses.example: All passengers must be aboard before the ferry leaves.
senses.exampleCN: 渡轮开动前所有乘客必须上船。
senses.why: The prefix a- means on, and board is the deck of a ship, so aboard is literally on the deck.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 a- 意为「在」，board 指船板、甲板，所以 aboard 字面就是「在甲板上」。

senses.title: Onto a vehicle
senses.titleCN: 上车、登船、登机
senses.definition: moving onto a ship, train or plane
senses.definitionCN: 移动到船、火车或飞机之上
senses.example: The crew helped the last two passengers aboard.
senses.exampleCN: 船员把最后两名乘客扶上了船。
senses.why: The same word serves both rest and motion, so it covers being on the deck and getting onto it.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词兼表静止与移动，所以既指在甲板上，也指登上甲板。

senses.title: In the greeting
senses.titleCN: 在欢迎语中
senses.definition: in welcome aboard, joining a team rather than a ship
senses.definitionCN: 在「welcome aboard」中，指加入一个团队而不只是登船
senses.example: Welcome aboard, the manager said to the new intern.
senses.exampleCN: 经理对新来的实习生说：欢迎加入。
senses.why: A vessel is a workplace too, so joining a crew widened into joining any team.
senses.whyCN: 船也是工作场所，于是「加入船员」扩展到「加入任何团队」。

intro.en: Aboard is a short English phrase frozen into one word: on board.
intro.cn: aboard 是由英语短语凝结成一个词的：on board。

items.en: bord meant a plank or the side of a ship.
items.cn: bord 意为木板或船舷。

items.en: abord meant on board a ship, with the prefix a- for on.
items.cn: abord 意为在船上，前缀 a- 表示「在」。

items.en: the spelling aboard settled and widened to trains and boats.
items.cn: 拼写 aboard 固定下来，意义扩展到火车与小艇。

items.en: with flight the word moved naturally to planes.
items.cn: 随着飞行出现，这个词自然移用到飞机上。

items.en: welcome aboard became a greeting for any new arrival.
items.cn: 「welcome aboard」成了对所有新来者的欢迎语。

note.en: The look-alike group is board and its compounds; the near-meaning group holds other place phrases for vehicles.
note.cn: 形近组是 board 及其复合词；近义组收其他表「在交通工具上」的说法。

entries.definition: A plank, a committee, or the act of getting on.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「木板、委员会、登乘」。

entries.definition: In or to a foreign country.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「在国外」，形近而义异。

entries.definition: The formal phrase for being on a vessel.
entries.definitionCN: 短语，义为「在船上」，较正式。

entries.definition: The two-word form of the same phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 短语，同义的两词形式。

entries.definition: On the surface of a vehicle.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「在……上」。

entries.definition: The air version of the same word.
entries.definitionCN: 短语，这个词在航空场景的用法。

entries.definition: To go on board a ship, then to begin something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「上船」，后引申为「着手」。

entries.definition: On land, away from the ship.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「在岸上」，是反义。

normalIntro.en: The hooks work from the two halves a- and board and from the phrases it lives in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从 a- 与 board 两个部件出发，也依靠它常处的短语。

normal.en: A- means on, board means plank, so aboard is on the planks.
normal.cn: a- 意为在，board 意为木板，所以 aboard 就是「在木板上」。

normal.en: The word covers both resting on a deck and climbing onto it.
normal.cn: 这个词兼指待在甲板上与登上甲板。

normal.en: Do not confuse aboard with abroad: one is a ship, one is a country.
normal.cn: 别把 aboard 与 abroad 弄混：一个指船，一个指国外。

normal.en: 「welcome aboard」 greets a new colleague as a new crew member.
normal.cn: 「welcome aboard」把新同事当新船员来欢迎。

normal.en: Embark keeps the same board and means going on a ship.
normal.cn: embark 含着同一个 board，指上船。

abstract.en: A gangplank laid from shore to deck is the picture behind the word.
abstract.cn: 一块从岸搭到甲板的跳板，是这个词背后的画面。

abstract.en: Any vehicle is a small floating world, so aboard fits all of them.
abstract.cn: 任何交通工具都是一个小小浮世，所以 aboard 通用于它们。

abstract.en: A ship and an office both take new arrivals aboard.
abstract.cn: 船与办公室都让人 aboard 进来。

examples.en: All passengers must be aboard before the ferry leaves.
examples.cn: 渡轮开动前所有乘客必须上船。

examples.en: The crew helped the last two passengers aboard.
examples.cn: 船员把最后两名乘客扶上了船。

examples.en: Welcome aboard, the manager said to the new intern.
examples.cn: 经理对新来的实习生说：欢迎加入。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额，宝的」——额，船板上那宝贝，就在船上。

root: 古英语 bord（木板、船舷）加前缀 a-（在……上）构成中古英语 abord，即「在甲板上」；同族词有 board、on board、embark。

sensesIntro.en: Being on the planks of a ship becomes getting onto it, and a ship crew widens into any team.
sensesIntro.cn: 待在船板上先是变成登上船板，船员一义又扩展到任何团队。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gangplank from shore to deck.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块从岸上搭到甲板的跳板。

branches.en: PLACE LINE: already standing on the deck.
branches.cn: 位置线：人已站在甲板上。

branches.en: MOTION LINE: stepping from shore onto the deck.
branches.cn: 移动线：从岸上迈到甲板上。

branches.en: TEAM LINE: a new crew member joins the vessel.
branches.cn: 团队线：新船员登上这条船。

branches.en: VEHICLE LINE: the same deck on trains and planes.
branches.cn: 交通工具线：火车与飞机也有同一块甲板。

branches.en: CONTRAST: ashore is the same trip in reverse.
branches.cn: 对照线：ashore 是同一趟行程的反向。

intro.en: A preposition prefix plus a word for plank, the shortest possible ship word.
intro.cn: 一个介词前缀加一个表「木板」的词，是最短的船上用语。

latinIntro.en: The prefix a- here is English on; board itself is Germanic, not Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 这里的前缀 a- 其实就是英语的 on；board 本身是日耳曼语词，并非拉丁语。

items.example: It looks alike but means elsewhere.

definition_zh: 废除；取消（法律、制度、习俗）
definition_en: to end a law, system or custom officially
core_image: 一纸法规被划掉，印章盖在废字上
scene: 议会在深夜投票，几百年的旧税种一夜之间没了。The country abolished the death penalty in nineteen eighty.
sceneCN: 这里 abolish 是「废除」（第 1 个义项：正式终止法律或制度）；句意为该国在一九八〇年废除了死刑。那枚盖在废字上的印章，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 动词：废除、取消（法律、制度、习俗等）

derivatives.zh: 加 -ition 构成，义为「废除、废止」
加 -ist 构成，义为「废奴主义者、主张废除者」
过去分词作形容词，义为「已废除的」

senses.title: To end a law or system
senses.titleCN: 废除法律或制度
senses.definition: officially ends a law, tax or institution
senses.definitionCN: 正式终止某项法律、税种或机构
senses.example: The country abolished the death penalty in nineteen eighty.
senses.exampleCN: 该国在一九八〇年废除了死刑。
senses.why: Latin abolere meant to destroy so that nothing remains, and law is what English most often destroys this way.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 abolere 意为彻底销毁、不留痕迹，英语最常这样处理的就是法律。

senses.title: To end a practice or custom
senses.titleCN: 取消习俗或做法
senses.definition: puts an end to a long-standing custom or practice
senses.definitionCN: 终结一种长期存在的习俗或做法
senses.example: The school abolished uniforms after years of protest.
senses.exampleCN: 经过多年抗议，学校取消了校服。
senses.why: A custom can be wiped out as cleanly as a rule, so the verb reaches everyday habits too.
senses.whyCN: 习俗也能像规章一样被抹掉，于是这个动词也触及日常习惯。

senses.title: In the noun form
senses.titleCN: 在名词形式中
senses.definition: the noun abolition names the ending, often of slavery
senses.definitionCN: 名词 abolition 指这种终止，常用于废奴
senses.example: The abolition of slavery took decades of campaigning.
senses.exampleCN: 废除奴隶制经过了几十年的奔走呼吁。
senses.why: The noun keeps the Latin participle stem, so abolition and abolish share one root but split into two word classes.
senses.whyCN: 名词保留了拉丁语分词词干，所以 abolition 与 abolish 同根却分成两个词类。

intro.en: Abolish is a formal Latin word, and its roots still carry the idea of wiping something out.
intro.cn: abolish 是个正式的拉丁语词，词根至今仍带着「抹去」的意思。

items.en: abolere meant to destroy or blot out, so that nothing survives.
items.cn: abolere 意为销毁、抹掉，使什么都不剩。

items.en: the past participle abolitus named a thing already wiped away.
items.cn: 过去分词 abolitus 指已被抹去之物。

items.en: French carried the verb on as abolir with the same force.
items.cn: 法语以 abolir 承接这个动词，力量不变。

items.en: English adopted it for repealing laws and institutions.
items.cn: 英语借入后用于废止法律与制度。

items.en: the word now ends customs and penalties as well as statutes.
items.cn: 如今它既终止法令，也终止习俗与刑罚。

note.en: The look-alike group is the abolition family; the near-meaning group holds other verbs of ending rules.
note.cn: 形近组是 abolition 词族；近义组收其他表示「终止规定」的动词。

entries.definition: The official ending of a law or system.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「废除」。

entries.definition: A person who campaigns to end a system.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「主张废除者、废奴主义者」。

entries.definition: Having been officially ended.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「已废除的」。

entries.definition: To make a surface shine; an unrelated verb.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「擦亮」，形近而无关。

entries.definition: To end a law by official vote.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「（经表决）废止法律」。

entries.definition: To call off something arranged, wider and looser.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「取消」，范围更宽。

entries.definition: To bring something to a stop, the plainest word.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「结束」，最朴素的说法。

entries.definition: To set a rule or system up in the first place.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「设立」，是反义。

normalIntro.en: The hooks follow the Latin root of destruction and the -ition noun.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子贴着表示「销毁」的拉丁词根与 -ition 名词。

normal.en: The root abolere meant to blot out, so abolish leaves no law behind.
normal.cn: 词根 abolere 意为抹掉，所以 abolish 之后不留法律。

normal.en: Abolish takes systems, not objects: you abolish slavery, not a cup.
normal.cn: abolish 的对象是制度而非物件：废的是奴隶制，不是杯子。

normal.en: Add -ition for the act, add -ist for the campaigner.
normal.cn: 加 -ition 成动作名词，加 -ist 指主张废除的人。

normal.en: Repeal needs a vote; abolish is the broader word for ending a whole system.
normal.cn: repeal 需经表决；abolish 更广，指终结整个制度。

normal.en: Abolish and establish are a pair: one builds a rule, one wipes it out.
normal.cn: abolish 与 establish 成对：一个立规，一个抹规。

abstract.en: A rubber stamp on the word void is the whole picture.
abstract.cn: 在「作废」二字上盖一枚印章，就是全部画面。

abstract.en: What is abolished is not broken but made not to exist.
abstract.cn: 被废除的东西不是被打坏，而是被弄得不存在。

abstract.en: Every abolition began as an argument someone lost.
abstract.cn: 每一次废除，都始于一场有人认输的辩论。

examples.en: The country abolished the death penalty in nineteen eighty.
examples.cn: 该国在一九八〇年废除了死刑。

examples.en: The school abolished uniforms after years of protest.
examples.cn: 经过多年抗议，学校取消了校服。

examples.en: Campaigners worked for the abolition of slavery.
examples.cn: 运动者致力于废除奴隶制。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿伯利是」——阿伯说，这条规矩利是不利，干脆废了。

root: 拉丁语 abolere（销毁、抹去）的过去分词 abolitus，经法语 abolir 进入英语；同族词有 abolition、abolitionist。

sensesIntro.en: Wiping something out of existence first hits laws and systems, then customs, and names the act in abolition.
sensesIntro.cn: 把东西抹得不存在，先落在法律与制度上，再到习俗，最后用 abolition 命名这个动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a statute struck through and stamped void.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条法规被划掉，盖上作废印。

branches.en: LAW LINE: a statute officially ended.
branches.cn: 法律线：法令被正式终止。

branches.en: CUSTOM LINE: a long habit put out of use.
branches.cn: 习俗线：长期习惯被停用。

branches.en: NOUN LINE: the act named as abolition.
branches.cn: 名词线：这个动作称为 abolition。

branches.en: CONTRAST: establish builds the same rule in reverse.
branches.cn: 对照线：establish 是反向建立同一条规定。

branches.en: RELATED: repeal is the voting-room version.
branches.cn: 关联线：repeal 是表决厅里的说法。

intro.en: The -ish verb ending arrives from French, while -ition and -ist build the nouns.
intro.cn: 动词词尾 -ish 来自法语，另用 -ition 与 -ist 造名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin abolere gave the stem abol-; French -ir and English -ish shaped the verb.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 abolere 提供词干 abol-；法语 -ir 与英语 -ish 塑成动词形式。

definition_zh: 非法的；违法的；不合规定的
definition_en: forbidden by law or by an official rule
core_image: 一道红线横在纸面上，脚一跨过去就被拦下
scene: 法庭门外，律师把一叠材料推回当事人手边，低声叮嘱这份合同不能签。Parking on this street is illegal after midnight.
sceneCN: 这里 illegal 是「违法的」（第 1 个义项：法律禁止）；句意为午夜后在这条街上停车是违法的。那条横在纸上的红线，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 形容词：非法的、违法的；不合规定的
名词（口语）：非法居留者；非法移民

derivatives.zh: 加 -ly 构成，义为「不法地、非法地」
名词，义为「违法性、非法状态」，由 illegal 加 -ity 构成
去掉否定前缀 il- 后的形容词，义为「合法的」
名词，义为「合法性」，是 illegality 的正面词

senses.title: Forbidden by law
senses.titleCN: 违法的：法律明文禁止
senses.definition: not allowed by the law of a country
senses.definitionCN: 被一个国家的法律所禁止
senses.example: Parking on this street is illegal after midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 午夜后在这条街上停车是违法的。
senses.why: Latin legalis came from lex, law; the negative prefix il- says the thing sits outside the law.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 legalis 出自 lex「法律」；否定前缀 il- 表示它站在法的外面。

senses.title: Against a game rule
senses.titleCN: 违规的：违反比赛或游戏规则
senses.definition: not permitted by the rules of a game or sport
senses.definitionCN: 不被某项比赛或运动的规则允许
senses.example: The referee whistled because the tackle was illegal.
senses.exampleCN: 裁判吹哨，因为那次抢断是违规的。
senses.why: A referee is a small legislator: the same prefix marks the player who steps outside the line.
senses.whyCN: 裁判就是小型的立法者，同一个否定前缀标记出越线的那名球员。

senses.title: Not allowed by an organization
senses.titleCN: 不合规定的：组织或单位内部禁止
senses.definition: banned by the official rules of a school, company or institution
senses.definitionCN: 被学校、公司或机构的正式规定所禁止
senses.example: Using a phone during the exam is illegal at this school.
senses.exampleCN: 在这所学校，考试时用手机是不合规定的。
senses.why: Forbid spreads from law to any written rule that binds a group of people.
senses.whyCN: 「禁止」从国家法律扩散到任何约束一群人的成文规定。

senses.title: A person without legal status
senses.titleCN: 非法居留者：没有合法身份的移民
senses.definition: a person who entered or stays in a country without legal permission
senses.definitionCN: 未经合法许可进入或停留在某国的人
senses.example: He worked for years as an illegal before the papers came through.
senses.exampleCN: 在证件办下来之前，他作为非法居留者打了好几年工。
senses.why: Names move from the act to the actor: the person whose presence lies outside the law takes the word itself.
senses.whyCN: 词从行为转到人身上：身处法律之外的那个人，就套用了这个词。

senses.title: Psychologically taboo
senses.titleCN: 心理禁忌：社会觉得不该碰
senses.definition: used loosely for something society feels you should not touch
senses.definitionCN: 口语中泛指社会认为不该去碰的事物
senses.example: Asking about a salary at dinner is almost illegal here.
senses.exampleCN: 在这里，饭桌上打听工钱几乎成了禁忌。
senses.why: The line drawn by law is borrowed for the unwritten line drawn by manners.
senses.whyCN: 法律划的那条线，被借用到礼俗所划的无形界线上。

intro.en: Illegal is the Latin word for law plus the negative prefix il-, which is in- worn down before l.
intro.cn: illegal 就是拉丁语的「法律」加上否定前缀 il-，也就是 in- 在 l 前面磨成的样子。

items.en: Latin lex, genitive legis, meant law and gave the whole legal family.
items.cn: 拉丁语 lex，属格 legis，意为「法律」，衍生出整个 legal 词族。

items.en: Legalis is derived from lex and describes what belongs to the law.
items.cn: legalis 由 lex 派生，意为「属于法律的」。

items.en: The prefix in- means not; before l it is written il-, as in illegal and illiterate.
items.cn: 前缀 in- 表示「不」；在 l 前写作 il-，如 illegal、illiterate。

items.en: Medieval French formed illegal as a mirror of legal and passed it into English.
items.cn: 中世纪法语照 legal 的样子造出 illegal，并传入英语。

items.en: In English the word first meant unlawful, and by Victorian times it also covered rules of games and schools.
items.cn: 英语中这个词最初只指违法，到维多利亚时代也覆盖比赛与学校的规定。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words with the same law root or the same negative il-; the near-meaning group holds words of prohibition.
note.cn: 形近组收同「法」词根或同用 il- 否定的词；近义组收表示禁止的词。

entries.definition: The adverb of the same word: in a way that breaks the law.
entries.definitionCN: 同词根的副词，义为「违法地」。

entries.definition: So badly written that it cannot be read; only the prefix is shared.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「字迹难辨」，只共用否定前缀 il-，词根不同。

entries.definition: Not following reason; shares the negative prefix but has a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不合逻辑」，共用否定前缀而词根不同。

entries.definition: Allowed by law; the same root without the negative prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「合法的」，同词根但去掉否定前缀。

entries.definition: Not permitted by law; a more formal synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不合法的」，更正式的同义词。

entries.definition: Relating to crime; stronger than illegal, since a crime has been committed.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「犯罪的」，比 illegal 更重，指已构成罪行。

entries.definition: Officially forbidden by a notice or an order.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「被禁止的」，多指通告或命令明令禁止。

entries.definition: Lawful and acceptable; the direct opposite in tone.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「合法的、正当的」，语气上的直接反义。

normalIntro.en: The hooks rest on the law root, the negative prefix and the everyday notices that use the word.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子依靠「法」词根、否定前缀和日常生活中随处可见的告示。

normal.en: il- says not, legal says law, so illegal is simply not-law.
normal.cn: il- 说「不」，legal 说「法」，illegal 就是不在法内。

normal.en: The same il- negates legible and logical, both meaning cannot.
normal.cn: 同一个 il- 也否定了 legible 与 logical，都是「不能」。

normal.en: Dropping the il- leaves legal, the honest twin of the word.
normal.cn: 去掉 il- 剩下 legal，正是这个词的正身。

normal.en: Illegal parking and illegal drugs are the two phrases news copy uses most.
normal.cn: illegal parking 与 illegal drugs 是新闻里最常见的两个搭配。

normal.en: It is illegal to do something is the pattern for signs and warnings.
normal.cn: 表示告示与警告时常用「做某事是违法的」这个句式。

abstract.en: Picture a line painted on the pavement: on this side you may stand, one step across and the word names you.
abstract.cn: 想象人行道上画了一条线：这边站着没事，跨过去一步，这个词就指着你。

abstract.en: Law is invisible, so the language gives it a visible edge, and illegal is the name of everything beyond that edge.
abstract.cn: 法律是无形的，语言便给它一条看得见的边，而 illegal 就是边外一切的名称。

abstract.en: The prefix is a small closed door: it does not describe the act, it simply refuses entry.
abstract.cn: 这个前缀像一扇小小关上的门：它不描述行为，只是拒绝放行。

examples.en: It is illegal to sell cigarettes to children.
examples.cn: 向儿童出售香烟是违法的。

examples.en: The company was fined for illegal dumping.
examples.cn: 这家公司因非法倾倒废料而被罚款。

examples.en: The referee ruled the move illegal and gave a free kick.
examples.cn: 裁判判定这个动作违规，判了一个任意球。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「衣离狗」——衣服离开狗半尺就乱了套，因为不许这么干

root: 拉丁语 lex/legis（法律）派生出 legalis，加否定前缀 in-（在 l 前写作 il-）得到 illegal；同族词有 legal、legally、illegality、illegible。

sensesIntro.en: Illegal starts at the statute book and then spreads to game rules, school rules and even social taboos.
sensesIntro.cn: illegal 从法典出发，再扩散到比赛规则、学校规定，甚至社会禁忌。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a red line on paper, with a foot stopped just before it.
core.cn: 核心意象：纸上一道红线，一只脚停在它前面。

branches.en: STATUTE: the law draws the line and forbids the act.
branches.cn: 法条线：法律画出界线，禁止该行为。

branches.en: RULE BOOKS: referees and schools borrow the same line.
branches.cn: 规则线：裁判与学校借用了同一条线。

branches.en: PERSON LINE: the actor takes the name of the act.
branches.cn: 人物线：行为者接过了行为的名。

branches.en: MANNER LINE: manners imitate law with no penalty attached.
branches.cn: 礼俗线：礼俗模仿法律，却没有处罚。

branches.en: CONTRAST: legal stands on the allowed side of the line.
branches.cn: 对照线：legal 站在被允许的那一侧。

intro.en: The word is a negative prefix plus a root meaning law, plus a plain adjective ending.
intro.cn: 这个词由否定前缀、意为「法」的词根和普通形容词词尾组成。

latinIntro.en: Lex and its stem leg- are the Latin source; the prefix in- supplies the denial.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的 lex 及其词干 leg- 是来源，前缀 in- 提供否定。

items.exampleCN: 它把 legal 变成 illegal。

items.example: It is the heart of legal and legislation.
items.exampleCN: 它是 legal 与 legislation 的核心。

items.example: It turns a noun into an adjective.
It is the base of the pair.
The prefix is shared, the root is not.
It shows how common the prefix is.
items.exampleCN: 它显示这个前缀有多常见。

items.example: It keeps the law root visible.
items.exampleCN: 它让「法」这个词根保持可见。

definition_zh: 不法地；非法地；违法地；违规地
definition_en: in a way that breaks the law or an official rule
core_image: 一只手绕开正门，从围墙上翻了过去
scene: 海关仓库的账本上少了一整页，调查员推断货物被偷偷运出了边境。The trucks were parked illegally along the whole street.
sceneCN: 这里 illegally 是「违法地」（第 1 个义项：以违背法律的方式）；句意为整条街上的卡车都违章停放着。那只绕过正门的手，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 副词：不法地、非法地；违规地

derivatives.zh: 去掉 -ly 得到的形容词，义为「违法的、非法的」
名词，义为「违法性」，与 illegally 同出一源
去掉否定前缀与 -ly 后的正面词，义为「合法的」

senses.title: Breaking the law
senses.titleCN: 违法地：以违背法律的方式
senses.definition: in a manner that breaks a law
senses.definitionCN: 以违反法律的方式
senses.example: The trucks were parked illegally along the whole street.
senses.exampleCN: 整条街上的卡车都违章停放着。
senses.why: The adverb adds -ly to the adjective illegal, so it describes how the action stands toward the law.
senses.whyCN: 副词在形容词 illegal 上加 -ly，于是它描述动作与法律的关系。

senses.title: Entering without permission
senses.titleCN: 非法入境地：未经许可越境
senses.definition: by entering or staying in a country without a legal right
senses.definitionCN: 未经合法权利进入或停留在某国
senses.example: They crossed the border illegally in the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在雨中非法越过了边境。
senses.why: Borders are laws drawn on the ground, and the adverb carries the same denial across them.
senses.whyCN: 边境就是画在地上的法律，这个副词把同一种否定带过了边界。

senses.title: Obtaining by forbidden means
senses.titleCN: 以非法手段获取：来路不正
senses.definition: by obtaining evidence, money or goods through a forbidden method
senses.definitionCN: 通过被禁止的手段取得证据、钱款或货物
senses.example: The judge threw out the illegally obtained confession.
senses.exampleCN: 法官排除了那份非法取得的供词。
senses.why: When the way of getting something is the problem, the adverb attaches to the method, not the person.
senses.whyCN: 当问题出在获取途径上，副词修饰的是手段，而不是人。

senses.title: Against competition rules
senses.titleCN: 违规地：违反比赛或行业规则
senses.definition: in a way that breaks the rules of a sport or a trade
senses.definitionCN: 以违反运动或行业规则的方式
senses.example: The club was punished for paying a player illegally.
senses.exampleCN: 这家俱乐部因违规支付球员报酬而受罚。
senses.why: The same manner word covers rule breaks as well as crimes, following the adjective it comes from.
senses.whyCN: 同样的方式副词也覆盖违规行为，而不只是犯罪，这沿袭了它的形容词。

intro.en: Illegally is an English build: Latin lex plus in-, then the adjective ending -al and the adverb ending -ly.
intro.cn: illegally 是英语自铸的词：拉丁语 lex 加 in-，再叠形容词词尾 -al 与副词词尾 -ly。

items.en: Lex, law, is the root that gives legality its whole family.
items.cn: lex 意为「法律」，是整个「合法」词族的根。

items.en: Medieval Latin already had illegalis, formed from in- and legalis.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语已有 illegalis，由 in- 与 legalis 构成。

items.en: French passed the adjective illegal into English in the late Middle Ages.
items.cn: 中世纪末法语把这个形容词 illegal 传入英语。

items.en: The adjective settled in English legal and official writing first.
items.cn: 这个形容词先在英语的法律与公文里扎根。

items.en: The adverb ending -ly was added in English, so adverbial use of the word is a later step.
items.cn: 副词词尾 -ly 是英语后期加的，词的副词用法也因此晚于形容词。

note.en: The look-alike group is the -ly adverb family of the same root; the near-meaning group holds other adverbs of wrongdoing.
note.cn: 形近组是同一词根的 -ly 副词族；近义组收其他表示不法行事的副词。

entries.definition: The adjective from which the adverb is built.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「违法的」，副词由它派生。

entries.definition: In a lawful manner; the same -ly against a different prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「合法地」，同一 -ly 但前缀相反。

entries.definition: A fixed phrase where the adverb modifies a participle.
entries.definitionCN: 固定短语，副词修饰分词。

entries.definition: The same prefix and the same -ly on a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 同前缀同词尾，但词根不同。

entries.definition: In a way not allowed by law; close in sense and more formal.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「不合法地」，意义接近而更正式。

entries.definition: In a mistaken or unjust way, weaker than illegally.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「错误地、不正当地」，语气弱于 illegally。

entries.definition: In a hidden way; the manner rather than the legality.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「秘密地」，说的是隐秘而非违法。

entries.definition: Without hiding anything; often the opposite style of acting.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「公开地」，做事风格常与之相反。

normalIntro.en: The hooks lean on the -ly ending, the negative prefix and the collocations of traffic and borders.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借 -ly 词尾、否定前缀以及交通与边境的常见搭配。

normal.en: Add -ly to illegal and you have told how the act was done.
normal.cn: 在 illegal 后面加 -ly，就交代了这件事是怎么做的。

normal.en: The il- never disappears; the denial travels with the -ly.
normal.cn: il- 始终不掉，否定随着 -ly 一起走。

normal.en: Park illegally is the first phrase learners meet.
normal.cn: 很多人最早遇到的就是 park illegally。

normal.en: Illegally obtained evidence is a phrase judges use in court.
normal.cn: illegally obtained evidence 是法官在庭上常用的说法。

normal.en: Every illegally hides an illegal behind it.
normal.cn: 每个 illegally 后面都站着一个 illegal。

abstract.en: The adjective paints a dark area; the adverb says that someone walked into it.
abstract.cn: 形容词画出那块暗区，副词则说有人走了进去。

abstract.en: Manner words are fingerprints: they show the style of the action, and here the style is denial of law.
abstract.cn: 方式副词像指纹，显示动作的风格，而这里的风格就是否认法律。

abstract.en: Two small letters, -ly, turn a verdict into a description of how someone moved.
abstract.cn: 两个字母的 -ly，把一个判决变成了对某人动作方式的描述。

examples.en: The vans were parked illegally outside the gate.
examples.cn: 货车违规停在大门外。

examples.en: He was charged with entering the country illegally.
examples.cn: 他被控非法入境。

examples.en: The court rejected the illegally recorded conversation.
examples.cn: 法院排除了那段非法录音的对话。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「衣离港里」——衣服离了港口就藏在里边，见不得光

root: 由拉丁语 lex（法律）派生的 legal，加否定前缀 in-（在 l 前作 il-）成 illegal，再叠副词词尾 -ly；同族词有 legal、legally、illegality。

sensesIntro.en: Illegally describes the manner of an act: the law, the border, the evidence or the rule book is crossed.
sensesIntro.cn: illegally 描述行事方式：越过了法律、边境、取证规矩或比赛章程。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand slips past the front door and climbs the wall instead.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手绕过正门，改从墙上翻过去。

branches.en: STATUTE LINE: the action breaks a written law.
branches.cn: 法条线：动作违反了成文法。

branches.en: BORDER LINE: the body crosses without permission.
branches.cn: 边境线：身体在未获许可时越界。

branches.en: METHOD LINE: the way of obtaining something is barred.
branches.cn: 手段线：获取事物的方式被禁止。

branches.en: RULE LINE: the manner breaks a sport or trade rule.
branches.cn: 规则线：方式违反了运动或行业规则。

branches.en: CONTRAST: legally does the same action on the allowed side.
branches.cn: 对照线：legally 做同样的动作，却站在允许的一侧。

intro.en: Illegally is three pieces of grammar stacked on one old root: negative, adjective, adverb.
intro.cn: illegally 是把三层语法叠在一个古老词根上：否定、形容词、副词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root lex supplies law; the negative prefix in- supplies the denial.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 lex 提供「法律」，否定前缀 in- 提供否定。

items.example: It is the first two letters.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个词的头两个字母。

items.example: It carries the meaning of law.

items.exampleCN: 它把 illegal 变成 illegally。

items.example: It shows the root at work.

definition_zh: 疾病；生病；病痛；病情
definition_en: the state of being unwell, or a particular disease
core_image: 一个人裹着毯子坐在床边，额头上贴着温度计
scene: 窗外的雨下了一整天，孩子没去上学，母亲在厨房里低声打电话请假。His illness kept him at home for three weeks.
sceneCN: 这里 illness 是「生病、疾病」（第 1 个义项：身体不适的状态）；句意为他的病让他在家待了三周。那条裹在身上的毯子，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 名词：疾病；生病；病痛；病情

derivatives.zh: 去掉名词后缀 -ness 得到的形容词，义为「生病的、不适的」
同义但不同的构词，义为「疾病」，形容词 sick 加 -ness
形容词 well 加 -ness 构成，义为「健康」，是 illness 的对照词

senses.title: The state of being unwell
senses.titleCN: 生病：身体不适的状态
senses.definition: the condition of being physically or mentally unwell
senses.definitionCN: 身体或精神不适的状况
senses.example: His illness kept him at home for three weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 他的病让他在家待了三周。
senses.why: The suffix -ness turns the adjective ill into a state, so the word names the condition itself.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ness 把形容词 ill 变成一种状态，这个词因此指疾病本身。

senses.title: A particular disease
senses.titleCN: 某种疾病：具体的病名
senses.definition: a specific disease with a name and a course
senses.definitionCN: 有名称、有病程的某种具体疾病
senses.example: She suffers from a rare illness of the joints.
senses.exampleCN: 她患有一种罕见的关节疾病。
senses.why: Countable use is the state cut into separate cases, each with its own name.
senses.whyCN: 可数用法是把「状态」切成一个个独立的病例，每个都有自己的名字。

senses.title: Mental or emotional trouble
senses.titleCN: 精神或情绪上的病
senses.definition: a disorder of the mind or of the emotions
senses.definitionCN: 精神或情绪方面的失调
senses.example: The clinic treats illness of the mind as seriously as broken bones.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所把心病看得和骨折一样严重。
senses.why: The English word never limited itself to the body, so the mind can be its subject too.
senses.whyCN: 这个英语词从来不限于身体，因此心智也可以作它的对象。

senses.title: A period of suffering
senses.titleCN: 病程：生病的那一段时间
senses.definition: a stretch of time during which someone is unwell
senses.definitionCN: 某人不适的一段时间
senses.example: Nothing was published during his long illness.
senses.exampleCN: 在他漫长的病程中，他什么也没有发表。
senses.why: A state that lasts becomes a period, and the word then marks a chapter of life.
senses.whyCN: 持续的状态会变成一段时间，这个词于是标记人生的一个段落。

intro.en: Illness is a plain English build: the Norse-derived adjective ill plus the native noun suffix -ness.
intro.cn: illness 是地道的英语构造：来自古诺斯的形容词 ill 加上本族名词后缀 -ness。

items.en: Old Norse illr meant bad or evil and came into northern English.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 illr 意为「坏的、恶的」，进入英格兰北部方言。

items.en: Middle English ille meant bad, and only later unwell in body.
items.cn: 中古英语 ille 意为「坏的」，后来才指身体不适。

items.en: The native suffix -nes formed abstract nouns of state, as in goodness.
items.cn: 本族后缀 -nes 构成表状态的名词，如 goodness。

items.en: By the eighteenth century illness was the ordinary noun for being unwell.
items.cn: 到十八世纪，illness 已成为「生病」的常用名词。

items.en: Medical writing then broadened it to any named disease and to mental conditions.
items.cn: 此后医学写作又把它扩展到任何有名称的疾病与精神状况。

note.en: The look-alike group is the -ness family of state nouns; the near-meaning group holds words for sickness.
note.cn: 形近组是同用 -ness 构成的状态名词；近义组收表示病痛的词。

entries.definition: Unwell; the adjective the noun is built on.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「生病的」，是名词的基础。

entries.definition: Health as a state; the same -ness with the opposite adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「健康」，同尾缀配反义形容词。

entries.definition: A state of feeling good; the suffix shown plain.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「幸福」，展示同款后缀。

entries.definition: A state of feeling low; same building pattern.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「悲伤」，构词方式相同。

entries.definition: The state of being sick; almost interchangeable, a little more old-fashioned.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「疾病」，几乎可互换，略旧式。

entries.definition: A medical condition with a cause and a name, more clinical than illness.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「疾病」，更偏医学，强调病因与病名。

entries.definition: A minor illness, often a long-running small complaint.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「小病」，多指长期的小毛病。

entries.definition: A disturbance of normal function, common in medical names.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「失调、紊乱」，常见于医学名称。

normalIntro.en: The hooks work on the -ness suffix, the Norse origin of ill and the medical collocations.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子围绕 -ness 后缀、ill 的古诺斯来源和医学搭配。

normal.en: Ill is sick, -ness makes it a state, so illness is the state of being ill.
normal.cn: ill 是「病」，-ness 把它变成状态，illness 就是生病这件事。

normal.en: The same -ness builds happiness and sadness at no extra cost.
normal.cn: 同一个 -ness 顺手就能造出 happiness 与 sadness。

normal.en: Illness came from the Norse word for bad, then narrowed to the body.
normal.cn: illness 源自诺斯语的「坏」，后来缩小到身体。

normal.en: Mental illness is the most common technical pairing today.
normal.cn: mental illness 是如今最常见的技术搭配。

normal.en: Recover from an illness is the phrase patients and doctors share.
normal.cn: recover from an illness 是病人和医生共用的句子。

abstract.en: A blanket over the shoulders is the picture: not pain, but a whole changed state.
abstract.cn: 披在肩上的毯子是画面：不是某一处疼，而是整个状态变了。

abstract.en: The suffix is a container, and the English keep dropping states into it: good, sad, sick.
abstract.cn: 这个后缀是个容器，英语不断把状态投进去：好、悲伤、生病。

abstract.en: Illness is time as much as flesh: it is measured in days away from work.
abstract.cn: illness 既关乎肉身也关乎时间：它是用请假天数来衡量的。

examples.en: Her illness was diagnosed as a mild infection.
examples.cn: 她的病被诊断为轻度感染。

examples.en: Long illness can change a family budget as much as a job loss.
examples.cn: 长期生病对一个家庭预算的影响不亚于失业。

examples.en: He kept reading throughout his illness.
examples.cn: 他在整个病程中一直在读书。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「衣呢死」——衣服呢，裹在被里像死了一样，正是病倒了

root: 由古诺斯语 illr（坏）进入英语作形容词 ill（生病的），加本族名词后缀 -ness 构成 illness；同族词有 ill、sickness、wellness。

sensesIntro.en: Illness runs from an unwell state through named diseases to mental trouble and to the period itself.
sensesIntro.cn: illness 从不适状态延伸到具体病名、精神困扰，再到生病的那段时间。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person wrapped in a blanket, thermometer on the forehead.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人裹着毯子，额头上贴着温度计。

branches.en: STATE LINE: the body is simply not well.
branches.cn: 状态线：身体就是不舒服。

branches.en: NAME LINE: a disease gets its own label.
branches.cn: 病名线：某种疾病获得自己的名称。

branches.en: MIND LINE: the trouble sits in the head and heart.
branches.cn: 心智线：问题出在头脑与情绪。

branches.en: TIME LINE: the state becomes a stretch of days.
branches.cn: 时间线：状态化成一段日子。

branches.en: CONTRAST: wellness names the same container full of health.
branches.cn: 对照线：wellness 用同一个容器装满健康。

intro.en: One old adjective plus a native suffix that turns qualities into states.
intro.cn: 一个古老形容词加上一个把性质变成状态的本族后缀。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin in illness; both parts are Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: illness 里没有拉丁语成分，两部分都来自日耳曼语。

items.example: It is the stem of the word.
It turns adjectives into state nouns.
items.exampleCN: 它把形容词变成状态名词。
它用同一个容器装健康。

items.example: It shows the suffix at work.

items.exampleCN: 另一个普通的 -ness 名词。
它与 -ness 构造形成对照。

definition_zh: 阐明；说明；举例说明；给（书）加插图
definition_en: to make something clear by examples or pictures
core_image: 讲台上的人拿起粉笔，在黑板上画了一个图
scene: 会议室里有人说不明白，讲者转过身在白板上画了三道箭头。Let me illustrate my point with a simple example.
sceneCN: 这里 illustrate 是「阐明、说明」（第 1 个义项：用例子或图把话说清楚）；句意为让我用一个简单的例子说明我的观点。白板上那几道箭头，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 动词：阐明、说明；举例说明；给书刊加插图

derivatives.zh: 加 -ion 构成，义为「说明、图解、插图」
加 -ive 构成，义为「说明性的、起例证作用的」
加 -or 构成，义为「插图画家」

senses.title: To make clear with examples
senses.titleCN: 阐明：用例子把话说清楚
senses.definition: to explain something by giving examples
senses.definitionCN: 用举例的方式解释某事
senses.example: Let me illustrate my point with a simple example.
senses.exampleCN: 让我用一个简单的例子说明我的观点。
senses.why: Latin lustrare means to make bright; to illustrate is to light the idea up with an example.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 lustrare 意为「使明亮」；illustrate 就是用例子把想法照亮。

senses.title: To add pictures
senses.titleCN: 配插图：给书刊加上图画
senses.definition: to supply a book or article with pictures
senses.definitionCN: 给书或文章配上图画
senses.example: The whole story is illustrated with ink drawings.
senses.exampleCN: 整个故事都配了水墨插图。
senses.why: Pictures do to a page what examples do to an argument: they make it bright.
senses.whyCN: 图画对篇幅做的事，正如例子对论证做的事：让一切明亮起来。

senses.title: To serve as an example
senses.titleCN: 作为例证：本身就是证明
senses.definition: to be an example of a general point
senses.definitionCN: 本身即是某个普遍观点的例子
senses.example: Her career illustrates how far talent can travel.
senses.exampleCN: 她的经历说明了才华能走多远。
senses.why: The verb can point outward and inward at once: the thing illustrates, and the illustrating is done by the thing.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词能同时向外与向内指：事物证明了道理，而证明正是由事物完成的。

senses.title: To make clear in an argument
senses.titleCN: 论证中解释清楚
senses.definition: to clarify a statement inside a discussion or text
senses.definitionCN: 在讨论或文章中把某个说法解释清楚
senses.example: The next chapter illustrates the rules with real case files.
senses.exampleCN: 下一章用真实案例把这些规则讲清楚。
senses.why: Academic writing took the verb as its lighting tool for difficult rules.
senses.whyCN: 学术写作把这个动词当作照亮难懂规则的工具。

intro.en: Illustrate goes back to Latin lustrare, to make bright, with the prefix in- intensifying it.
intro.cn: illustrate 追溯到拉丁语 lustrare「使明亮」，前缀 in- 起加强作用。

items.en: Lustrum was a purifying sacrifice; the family of lustrare grew from light and cleansing.
items.cn: lustrum 是一种净化的献祭，lustrare 一族由「光」与「洁净」生长出来。

items.en: Illustrare meant to light up, to make clear, and also to make famous.
items.cn: illustrare 意为「照亮、使人明白」，也表示「使著名」。

items.en: Church writers used illustratio for mental enlightenment.
items.cn: 教会作者用 illustratio 表示心智上的启发。

items.en: English took the verb to mean making an idea clear.
items.cn: 英语借入这个动词，表示把想法说明白。

items.en: Printed books gave the verb its second life: to add pictures to a page.
items.cn: 印刷书籍给了它第二次生命：给书页添上图画。

note.en: The look-alike group is the -strate verb family; the near-meaning group holds verbs of explaining.
note.cn: 形近组是同一词族的动词；近义组收表示解释的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for a picture or an example that explains.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「插图、说明」。

entries.definition: Serving as an example; the adjective of the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「说明性的」。

entries.definition: A person who draws pictures for books.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「插图画家」。

entries.definition: To block or annoy; the ending is shared, the root is not.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使受挫」，词尾相同而词根不同。

entries.definition: The plain everyday verb for making something clear.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「解释」，最日常的说法。

entries.definition: To show clearly by evidence or by performing it.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「演示、证明」，靠证据或操作来显示。

entries.definition: To remove confusion from a statement.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「澄清」，专指消除混淆。

entries.definition: To show in a picture or in words; close to the drawing sense.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「描绘」，接近配图那个义项。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the picture sense, the light root and the -ate verb pattern.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借「图画」义、表「光」的词根以及 -ate 动词形式。

normal.en: Illustrate is linked to light: an example lights up your meaning.
normal.cn: illustrate 与「光」相连：例子把你的意思照亮。

normal.en: The verb ends in -ate, like demonstrate and calculate.
normal.cn: 这个动词以 -ate 结尾，与 demonstrate、calculate 一样。

normal.en: Books that are illustrated have pictures on the pages.
normal.cn: 被 illustrate 过的书，页面上就有了图画。

normal.en: Illustrate a point is the phrase in debates and essays.
normal.cn: illustrate a point 是辩论与作文里的常用搭配。

normal.en: The noun illustration keeps the same meaning in two forms.
normal.cn: 名词 illustration 用两种形式保留了同一个意思。

abstract.en: Imagine a torch: every example the speaker gives is one more beam on the dark board.
abstract.cn: 想象一支手电：讲者每举一个例子，就在暗板上多打一道光。

abstract.en: Two senses share one logic, since a picture is just an example in ink.
abstract.cn: 两个义项共享同一逻辑，因为图画不过是墨做的例子。

abstract.en: To illustrate is to lend your voice a second channel, showing rather than telling.
abstract.cn: illustrate 是给声音配第二条通道：演示而不是陈述。

examples.en: The teacher illustrated the rule with a story from her own school.
examples.cn: 老师用自己上学时的一个故事说明了这条规则。

examples.en: The report is illustrated with photographs from the border.
examples.cn: 这份报告配有边境地区的照片。

examples.en: His career illustrates the value of patience.
examples.cn: 他的经历说明了耐心的价值。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「以了斯特瑞特」——以了斯（丝）特（别）瑞（锐）特（别）地画出箭头讲清楚

root: 来自拉丁语 illustrare（照亮、使明白），由 in-（加强）+ lustrare（使明亮）构成；同族词有 illustration、illustrative、illustrator、lustre。

sensesIntro.en: Illustrate moves from lighting up an argument to adding pictures, and to being an example oneself.
sensesIntro.cn: illustrate 从照亮论证走到添加图画，再走到自身即为例子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: chalk arrows drawn on a dark board until the idea glows.
core.cn: 核心意象：在暗板上画出粉笔箭头，直到想法亮起来。

branches.en: LIGHT LINE: examples carry light to a difficult rule.
branches.cn: 光线条：例子把光带到难懂的规则上。

branches.en: PICTURE LINE: ink drawings do the same work on the page.
branches.cn: 图画线：水墨插画在纸面上做同样的工作。

branches.en: PROOF LINE: the thing itself becomes the example.
branches.cn: 证明线：事物本身成为了例子。

branches.en: SPEECH LINE: the speaker turned words into a diagram.
branches.cn: 言语线：讲者把话变成一张图。

branches.en: CONTRAST: telling says it, illustrating shows it.
branches.cn: 对照线：陈述是说出来，illustrate 是显示出来。

intro.en: A Latin verb of light with an intensive prefix and a common verb ending.
intro.cn: 一个关于光的拉丁动词，带加强前缀和常见的动词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Both pieces are Latin: in- intensifying and lustrare, to make bright.
latinIntro.cn: 两部分都是拉丁语：加强意义的 in- 与「使明亮」的 lustrare。

items.example: It is worn down to il- in illustrate.
items.exampleCN: 在 illustrate 里它磨成了 il-。

items.example: It links the word to lustre.
items.exampleCN: 它把这个词与 lustre 连在一起。

items.example: It keeps the light idea bare.
items.exampleCN: 它赤裸地保留了「光」的意思。

items.example: It is the meaning, not the root.
items.exampleCN: 它只与意义相近，不同词根。
它与该词共用动词框架。

latinEntries.meaning: to light up, to make clear

definition_zh: 插图；图解；说明；例证
definition_en: a picture in a book, or an example that explains something
core_image: 一页书上的图画，旁边排着几行说明文字
scene: 图书馆里，孩子们围坐在大书前，手指着一幅画了虫子的图。The illustration on page ten shows how the pump works.
sceneCN: 这里 illustration 是「插图」（第 1 个义项：书中的图画）；句意为第十页的插图展示了水泵的工作原理。那幅排在文字旁的画，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 名词：插图、图画；图解；说明；例证

derivatives.zh: 去掉 -ion 得到的动词，义为「阐明、说明、加插图」
加 -ive 构成，义为「说明性的、举例用的」
加 -or 构成，义为「插图画家」

senses.title: A picture in a book
senses.titleCN: 插图：书里的图画
senses.definition: a picture that appears in a book or magazine
senses.definitionCN: 出现在书刊中的图画
senses.example: The illustration on page ten shows how the pump works.
senses.exampleCN: 第十页的插图展示了水泵的工作原理。
senses.why: The Latin noun illustratio means a lighting up, and a printed picture lights up the text beside it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁名词 illustratio 意为「照亮」，而书中的图画正是照亮旁边的文字。

senses.title: An example that explains
senses.titleCN: 例证：用来说明的事例
senses.definition: an example used to make an idea clear
senses.definitionCN: 用来说明某个观点的例子
senses.example: The flood is a striking illustration of how fast a river can change.
senses.exampleCN: 这次洪水是河水能多快改道的一个惊人例证。
senses.why: One picture and one example do the same job: both are a beam of light on an abstract rule.
senses.whyCN: 一幅图和一个例子做同一件事：都是照在抽象规则上的一束光。

senses.title: The act of explaining
senses.titleCN: 说明：阐明这一行为
senses.definition: the act of making something clear
senses.definitionCN: 把某事讲清楚的行为
senses.example: The matter is too complex for brief illustration.
senses.exampleCN: 这件事太复杂，难以简要说明。
senses.why: The abstract sense keeps the verb inside the noun: not the picture, but the lighting.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义把动词藏进名词里：不是图画，而是照亮的过程。

senses.title: The art of drawing for books
senses.titleCN: 插图艺术：为书刊作画的行业
senses.definition: the craft or profession of drawing pictures for publication
senses.definitionCN: 为出版物作画的手艺或职业
senses.example: She studied illustration in art school and now draws for magazines.
senses.exampleCN: 她在美术学校学插图，现在给杂志画画。
senses.why: When a craft names itself after its product, the noun becomes a profession.
senses.whyCN: 当一门手艺用它的成品来命名，这个名词就成了一种职业。

intro.en: Illustration is the Latin noun of action behind illustrate, still carrying the idea of light.
intro.cn: illustration 是 illustrate 背后的拉丁动作名词，至今仍带着「光」的意象。

items.en: Lustrum and lustrare tied cleansing to brightness in Roman ritual.
items.cn: 在罗马仪式里，lustrum 与 lustrare 把净化与明亮绑在一起。

items.en: Illustratio meant a making bright, often of the mind.
items.cn: illustratio 意为「使明亮」，多指心智上的启发。

items.en: Old French passed the noun to English in the medieval period.
items.cn: 中古时期，古法语把这个名词传给英语。

items.en: With printed books the noun became a picture on a page.
items.cn: 随着印刷书籍出现，这个名词变成了书页上的图画。

items.en: In modern times it also names the craft of drawing for publication.
items.cn: 近代它又指为出版物作画的手艺。

note.en: The look-alike group is the illustration word family; the near-meaning group holds kinds of explanatory image and example.
note.cn: 形近组是 illustration 词族；近义组收说明性图像与例证的词。

entries.definition: The verb from which the noun is formed.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，名词由它构成。

entries.definition: Serving as an example or a picture.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「说明性的」。

entries.definition: The person who draws the pictures.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「插图画家」。

entries.definition: A false perception; only the spelling looks alike, the root is different.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「幻觉」，只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: The plain word for an image on a page or a wall.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「图画」，最普通的说法。

entries.definition: A drawing of parts and connections rather than a scene.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「图解」，画的是部件与关系而非场景。

entries.definition: The verbal twin of a picture when explaining.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「例子」，解释时的口头对应物。

entries.definition: The formal label for a numbered illustration in a text.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「图」，正文中对编号插图的正式称呼。

normalIntro.en: The hooks tie the noun to the light root, to picture books and to the example sense.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把名词连到「光」词根、图画书与例证义。

normal.en: Illustration ends in -ion, the usual sign of a noun of action.
normal.cn: illustration 以 -ion 结尾，这是动作名词的常见标志。

normal.en: Every illustration is a small light held up to the text.
normal.cn: 每一幅插图都是一盏举向文字的小灯。

normal.en: Children meet the word on the first page of a picture book.
normal.cn: 孩子们在图画书的第一页就遇上这个词。

normal.en: By way of illustration is the phrase lecturers use before an example.
normal.cn: 讲课的人举例子前常说 by way of illustration。

normal.en: The plural illustrations covers pictures, diagrams and examples at once.
normal.cn: 复数 illustrations 同时涵盖图画、图解和例子。

abstract.en: Think of the noun as a beam, not a bulb: it is the light delivered, not the thing shining.
abstract.cn: 把这个名词想成一束光而不是灯泡：它是送出的光，而不是发光的物体。

abstract.en: A picture on paper and an example in speech are the same gift in two materials.
abstract.cn: 纸上的图画与口头上的例子，是同样一份礼物用了两种材料。

abstract.en: Where words fail, an illustration steps in and does the explaining without a sentence.
abstract.cn: 文字失效之处，插图接手，不用一句完整的话就完成了说明。

examples.en: Each chapter opens with a full-page illustration.
examples.cn: 每一章都以一整页插图开始。

examples.en: The case is a clear illustration of how rumours spread.
examples.cn: 这个案例清楚地说明了流言是怎样传播的。

examples.en: She works in illustration and has drawn for many magazines.
examples.cn: 她从事插图工作，为许多杂志画过画。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「以了斯吹神」——以了斯（丝）吹出一幅神气的画

root: 拉丁语 illustratio（照亮、阐明）来自 illustrare（照亮），后者由 in-（加强）+ lustrare（使明亮）构成；同族词有 illustrate、illustrative、illustrator、lustre。

sensesIntro.en: Illustration covers the picture, the example, the act of explaining and the craft that draws for books.
sensesIntro.cn: illustration 涵盖图画、例证、阐明这一行为，以及为书刊作画的行业。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an inked picture sitting beside a line of text, lighting it up.
core.cn: 核心意象：一幅墨线画挨着一行字，把它照亮。

branches.en: PAGE LINE: the picture sits inside the printed book.
branches.cn: 书页线：图画处在印刷书页之中。

branches.en: EXAMPLE LINE: an event stands in for the rule.
branches.cn: 例证线：一个事件替规则出场。

branches.en: ACTION LINE: the name points at the act of lighting up.
branches.cn: 动作线：名称指向「照亮」这一行为。

branches.en: CRAFT LINE: the art itself takes the same name.
branches.cn: 手艺线：这门艺术本身取得了同一个名称。

branches.en: CONTRAST: a picture is a noun, illustrating is the verb behind it.
branches.cn: 对照线：图画是名词，illustrating 是它背后的动词。

intro.en: The noun keeps the Latin light root and adds two suffixes that mark action and result.
intro.cn: 这个名词保留拉丁「光」词根，再叠两个标记动作与结果的后缀。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb illustrare supplies both the root and the idea of brightness.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁动词 illustrare 提供词根，也提供明亮这一意象。

items.example: It is worn down from in-.
It is the core of the word.
It comes from the Latin verb.
It is the closest label type.
items.exampleCN: 它是最接近的图类名称。

definition_zh: 图像；形象；印象；意象；肖像
definition_en: a picture of someone or something, or the impression people have
core_image: 镜面里映出的那张脸，与真人一模一样
scene: 展厅的灯一盏盏亮起来，墙上的照片被照得发白，人们安静地走过去看。The image on the screen was sharper than the print.
sceneCN: 这里 image 是「图像」（第 1 个义项：所见到的画面）；句意为屏幕上的图像比打印出来的更清楚。镜子里的那张脸，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 名词：图像、映像；形象；印象；意象
动词（书面）：描绘；想象；反映

derivatives.zh: 与 image 同根，义为「想象」，由拉丁 imaginari 而来
同根名词，义为「想象力、想象的事物」
同根形容词，义为「虚构的、想象中的」
同根形容词，义为「富有想象力的」

senses.title: A picture of something
senses.titleCN: 图像：所见或拍下的画面
senses.definition: a picture of a person or thing, seen, drawn or photographed
senses.definitionCN: 看到、画出或拍摄下的人或物的画面
senses.example: The image on the screen was sharper than the print.
senses.exampleCN: 屏幕上的图像比打印出来的更清楚。
senses.why: Latin imago meant a likeness, a copy that looks back at you from a mirror.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 imago 意为「相似之物」，是从镜子里回看你的复制品。

senses.title: How others see you
senses.titleCN: 形象：别人对你的看法
senses.definition: the impression that a person or company gives to the public
senses.definitionCN: 一个人或公司留给公众的印象
senses.example: The minister worked hard to repair his image after the scandal.
senses.exampleCN: 丑闻之后，这位部长努力修补自己的形象。
senses.why: A likeness moved from mirrors to minds: what people picture when your name is spoken.
senses.whyCN: 「相似之物」从镜子走进心里：人们听到你名字时脑中浮现的画面。

senses.title: A mental picture
senses.titleCN: 意象：脑海中浮现的画面
senses.definition: a picture formed in the mind, often by words in a poem
senses.definitionCN: 心中形成的画面，常见于诗歌用词
senses.example: The poet builds an image of winter from smoke and ice.
senses.exampleCN: 诗人用烟与冰搭出一个冬天的意象。
senses.why: Poetry uses the word for the thing seen and for the thing pictured in the reader.
senses.whyCN: 诗歌既用这个词指所见的物，也指读者心中所绘的图。

senses.title: A religious likeness
senses.titleCN: 神像：宗教中的塑像或画像
senses.definition: a statue or painting of a holy figure
senses.definitionCN: 圣像、雕像或画像
senses.example: Pilgrims knelt before the image of the saint.
senses.exampleCN: 朝圣者跪在圣徒像前。
senses.why: The oldest use is the statue that stands in for something invisible.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的用法，即代替不可见者而立的雕像。

senses.title: A likeness in a surface
senses.titleCN: 映像：镜面或水面映出的样子
senses.definition: the reflection seen in a mirror, a screen or still water
senses.definitionCN: 镜子、屏幕或静水中映出的样子
senses.example: She saw her own image in the dark window.
senses.exampleCN: 她在暗窗前看见自己的映像。
senses.why: The physical mirror is the oldest and most literal home of the word.
senses.whyCN: 具体的镜面是这个词最古老也最字面的归宿。

intro.en: Image descends from Latin imago, a likeness, and is a close cousin of imitate.
intro.cn: image 源自拉丁语 imago「相似之物」，与 imitate 是近亲。

items.en: Imago meant a likeness, a mask or a statue, and often the image of an ancestor.
items.cn: imago 意为「相似之物、面具、雕像」，常指祖先的像。

items.en: The genitive imaginem gave the stem imagin- that English words share.
items.cn: 属格 imaginem 给出词干 imagin-，英语诸词共用这个干。

items.en: Old French passed the word into English after the Norman period.
items.cn: 诺曼时期之后，古法语把这个词传入英语。

items.en: In Middle English it covered statues, reflections and mental pictures.
items.cn: 中古英语中，它兼指雕像、倒影与心中之像。

items.en: With film and later screens, the picture sense became the everyday one.
items.cn: 随着电影与后来的屏幕，画面这一义成为日常用法。

note.en: The look-alike group is the imagin- family; the near-meaning group holds words for pictures and reputations.
note.cn: 形近组是 imagin- 词族；近义组收表示画面与名声的词。

entries.definition: To form a picture in the mind; the sister verb.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「想象」，同根的姊妹词。

entries.definition: The power of forming pictures in the mind.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「想象力」。

entries.definition: Existing only in the mind, not in reality.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「虚构的、想象的」。

entries.definition: A copy made by imitating; shares the likeness idea.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「仿制品」，共用「相似」之意。

entries.definition: The plain everyday word for a drawing or photograph.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「图画、照片」，最日常的说法。

entries.definition: The view others hold of you, close to the image sense.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「名声」，接近形象一义。

entries.definition: A resemblance or a portrait; close to the oldest sense.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「相似之处、画像」，接近最古老的义项。

entries.definition: A deliberate picture of a particular person.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「肖像」，专指为某人画的像。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the mirror sense, the imagin- family and the media sense.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借助映象义、imagin- 词族以及媒体中的画面义。

normal.en: An image is what a mirror gives back, only smoother.
normal.cn: image 就是镜子还回来的那个东西，只是更光滑。

normal.en: Imagination is the workshop, an image is the thing made there.
normal.cn: imagination 是车间，image 是那里做出来的东西。

normal.en: The public image is simply the picture strangers carry of you.
normal.cn: public image 就是陌生人随身带着的那张你的照片。

normal.en: Image and imitate share the likeness idea of the Latin root.
normal.cn: image 与 imitate 共用拉丁词根那「相似」的意思。

normal.en: Image quality is the phrase on every camera box.
normal.cn: image quality 是每个相机盒子上都印着的词。

abstract.en: The word moves from glass to mind: first what the mirror shows, then what people believe.
abstract.cn: 这个词从玻璃走进心里：先是镜子显示的东西，后是人们相信的东西。

abstract.en: An image is a likeness that has won trust and no longer needs proof.
abstract.cn: 形象是一种已赢得信任的相似之物，不再需要证据。

abstract.en: Poets and advertisers both work with images, and both know a picture is faster than an argument.
abstract.cn: 诗人与广告人都在处理意象，都知道一张画面比一段论证更快。

examples.en: The satellite sent back a clear image of the coast.
examples.cn: 卫星传回了海岸的清晰图像。

examples.en: The company spent millions on its brand image.
examples.cn: 这家公司花了数百万来塑造品牌形象。

examples.en: She turned away so that her image would not be caught in the glass.
examples.cn: 她转过身，免得映像被玻璃照出来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一迷机」——一台迷住人的机器，映出画面

root: 拉丁语 imago（属格 imaginem，意为「相似之物、像」）经古法语进入英语；同族词有 imagine、imagination、imaginary、imitative。

sensesIntro.en: Image begins with a likeness in stone or glass and reaches the picture people hold in their heads.
sensesIntro.cn: image 从石头或玻璃上的像出发，延伸到人们脑中的画面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a face in a mirror answering your own.
core.cn: 核心意象：镜中一张脸回应着你的脸。

branches.en: SCREEN LINE: a picture on paper or on a display.
branches.cn: 屏幕线：纸面或显示屏上的画面。

branches.en: PUBLIC LINE: the likeness lives in other minds.
branches.cn: 公众线：那幅像活在他人心里。

branches.en: POETRY LINE: the mind draws a picture from words.
branches.cn: 诗意线：心从文字中绘出画面。

branches.en: OLD LINE: statue and mirror keep the literal sense.
branches.cn: 古老线：雕像与镜面保留了字面义。

branches.en: CONTRAST: reputation is the same picture with a judgement attached.
branches.cn: 对照线：reputation 是同一幅画加上了评价。

intro.en: A Latin noun stem, plain in English and fruitful for the whole imagin- family.
intro.cn: 一个拉丁名词词干，在英语中形态朴素，却生出了整个 imagin- 词族。

latinIntro.en: The stem imagin- comes straight from imago, imaginis, a likeness.
latinIntro.cn: 词干 imagin- 直接来自 imago, imaginis「相似之物」。

items.example: It is the core of image.

items.exampleCN: 它是这个英语名词的收尾。

items.example: It turns the stem into a verb.
It covers the statue sense too.
It is one kind of image.

definition_zh: 想象力；想象；想象的事物；创造力
definition_en: the ability to form pictures and new ideas in the mind
core_image: 孩子闭上眼睛，在墙角搭起一座并不存在的城堡
scene: 熄灯后的宿舍里，孩子们还在小声讲故事，情节越编越离奇。It takes imagination to explain a machine without a diagram.
sceneCN: 这里 imagination 是「想象力」（第 1 个义项：在脑中造出画面的能力）；句意为不用图示就讲清一台机器，是需要想象力的。墙角那座不存在的城堡，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 名词：想象力；想象；想象的事物；创造力

derivatives.zh: 去掉 -ation 得到的动词，义为「想象、设想」
同根形容词，义为「虚构的、想象中的」
加 -ive 构成，义为「富有想象力的」
同根名词，义为「图像、形象」

senses.title: The power to picture things
senses.titleCN: 想象力：在脑中造出画面的能力
senses.definition: the ability to form pictures and ideas that are not present
senses.definitionCN: 在脑中出现眼前并不存在的事物之画面的能力
senses.example: It takes imagination to explain a machine without a diagram.
senses.exampleCN: 不用图示就讲清一台机器，是需要想象力的。
senses.why: The Latin verb imaginari became a noun of action: the act of forming pictures turned into the power of doing it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词 imaginari 变成动作名词：作画的行为变成了作画的能力。

senses.title: Creativity of an artist
senses.titleCN: 创造力：艺术家构思新事物的本领
senses.definition: the creative power that produces new works and new designs
senses.definitionCN: 产出新作品与新设计的创造力量
senses.example: The film shows an imagination that no studio budget could contain.
senses.exampleCN: 这部影片显示的创造力，任何片厂的预算都装不下。
senses.why: When the power turns outward into products, the word names talent rather than a habit of mind.
senses.whyCN: 当这种能力向外变成作品，这个词就指才华，而不只是思维习惯。

senses.title: Things that are only imagined
senses.titleCN: 想象的事物：只存在于想象中的东西
senses.definition: things that exist only in the mind and not in the world
senses.definitionCN: 只存在于心里、现实中并不存在的事物
senses.example: The monsters in the letter turned out to be pure imagination.
senses.exampleCN: 信里那些怪物原来纯属想象。
senses.why: The same noun switches from the workshop to its output, so the products are also called imagination.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词从车间转指产品，于是成品也被叫作「想象」。

senses.title: The ability to understand others
senses.titleCN: 体察力：设身处地理解别人
senses.definition: the ability to enter the feelings and situation of others
senses.definitionCN: 设身处地体会他人的处境与感受的能力
senses.example: A good nurse needs imagination as much as skill.
senses.exampleCN: 好护士需要的体察力不亚于技术。
senses.why: To picture the life of another person is the same mental act applied to a human being rather than a design.
senses.whyCN: 把另一个人的生活成像，是同一心理活动用在人身上而非设计上。

intro.en: Imagination is the Latin noun of action behind imagine, built on the same likeness root as image.
intro.cn: imagination 是 imagine 背后的拉丁动作名词，建在与 image 相同的「相似」词根上。

items.en: Imago, a likeness, gave the whole imagin- family its root.
items.cn: imago「相似之物」给整个 imagin- 词族提供了词根。

items.en: Imaginari meant to picture something to oneself in the mind.
items.cn: imaginari 意为「在心中为自己描绘某物」。

items.en: Imaginatio was the act of picturing, used in late Latin philosophy.
items.cn: imaginatio 指「成像」这一行为，见于晚期拉丁哲学。

items.en: English borrowed it through French for mental image making.
items.cn: 英语经法语借入，指在心中造像。

items.en: Romantic writers raised it to the highest name for creative power.
items.cn: 浪漫主义作者把它推举为创造力的最高名号。

note.en: The look-alike group is the imagin- noun family; the near-meaning group holds words for creative power.
note.cn: 形近组是 imagin- 名词族；近义组收表示创造力的词。

entries.definition: The verb from which the noun is formed.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，名词由它构成。

entries.definition: Existing only in the mind.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「虚构的、想象中的」。

entries.definition: Full of imagination; describes a person or work.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「富有想象力的」。

entries.definition: A likeness or picture; the concrete noun of the family.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「图像、形象」，词族中的具体名词。

entries.definition: The general power to produce something new.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「创造力」，泛指产出新事物的能力。

entries.definition: A story or world made up by the mind.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「幻想」，指脑中编出的世界。

entries.definition: The act of creating something new, often practical.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「发明」，多指实用之物。

entries.definition: A forward-looking picture of what could be, close in sense.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「远见、构想」，意义接近但更前瞻。

normalIntro.en: The hooks tie the noun to the -ation ending, the imagine verb and the phrase about capture.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把名词连到 -ation 词尾、动词 imagine 以及 capture 相关短语。

normal.en: Imagination is imagine in a noun coat: same meaning, different job.
normal.cn: imagination 是 imagine 穿上了名词的外套：意思相同，职务不同。

normal.en: The -ation ending marks it as an action grown into a power.
normal.cn: 结尾的 -ation 标记它由动作长成一种能力。

normal.en: Use your imagination is what teachers say before a writing task.
normal.cn: 写作课开始前，老师总说 use your imagination。

normal.en: A story that captures the imagination holds the whole world still.
normal.cn: capture the imagination 的故事能让全世界静下来。

normal.en: Whatever is only in the head is called a figment of the imagination.
normal.cn: 只存在于脑子里的东西，被叫作 figment of the imagination。

abstract.en: Picture a child drawing a castle in the corner: nothing is there, and the castle is real to the child.
abstract.cn: 想象一个孩子在墙角画城堡：那里什么都没有，城堡对孩子却是真的。

abstract.en: The word holds both the workshop and its goods, the power and the things it makes.
abstract.cn: 这个词同时装着车间与货物，既指能力，也指它造出的东西。

abstract.en: Without it, every machine would look like the diagram and never like the idea behind it.
abstract.cn: 没有它，每台机器都只像一张图，永远不像图背后的想法。

examples.en: Her imagination turned the bare room into a ship at sea.
examples.cn: 她的想象力把空荡的房间变成了一艘海上之船。

examples.en: The idea caught the public imagination at once.
examples.cn: 这个想法立刻抓住了公众的心。

examples.en: The ghost in the story is pure imagination.
examples.cn: 故事里的鬼纯属想象。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一美的内神」——一台美的内里的神，全靠想象

root: 拉丁语 imaginari（在心中描绘）的名词形式 imaginatio，词根 imago（相似之物）；同族词有 image、imagine、imaginary、imaginative。

sensesIntro.en: Imagination names the power, the artist craft, the made-up things and the gift of entering other lives.
sensesIntro.cn: imagination 可指这种能力、艺术家的创造力、被想象出来的事物，以及进入他人生活的体察力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a child drawing a castle in a corner where nothing stands.
core.cn: 核心意象：孩子在空无一物的墙角画出一座城堡。

branches.en: POWER LINE: the everyday ability to picture.
branches.cn: 能力线：日常用品般的成像能力。

branches.en: CRAFT LINE: the power turned into finished works.
branches.cn: 才华线：能力变成完成的作品。

branches.en: OBJECT LINE: the made-up thing takes the name.
branches.cn: 对象线：编造之物借用了这个名字。

branches.en: HEART LINE: picturing another person and feeling with them.
branches.cn: 共情线：为他人成像并与之共感。

branches.en: CONTRAST: memory pictures what was, imagination pictures what could be.
branches.cn: 对照线：记忆画已成之事，想象画可能之事。

intro.en: A likeness root with a verb ending and then a noun ending, so the noun sits one step away from image.
intro.cn: 「相似」词根先加动词词尾再加名词词尾，名词因此离 image 只有一步。

latinIntro.en: Imago supplies the root; Latin added -inari for the verb and -atio for the noun.
latinIntro.cn: imago 提供词根；拉丁语加 -inari 成动词，加 -atio 成名词。

items.example: It is the core of the family.

items.exampleCN: 它覆盖艺术创造的一面。

definition_zh: 想象；设想；猜想；料想
definition_en: to form a picture or an idea in your mind
core_image: 一个人望着窗外，在脑子里先看到了明天的车站
scene: 车里安静，他闭着眼，把航班的路线在脑中走了一遍。Imagine the street without any cars and the noise simply disappears.
sceneCN: 这里 imagine 是「想象」（第 1 个义项：在脑中形成画面）；句意为想象一下这条街上没有车，噪音就完全消失了。闭眼在脑中走的那条路线，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 动词：想象、设想；猜想、料想

derivatives.zh: 加 -ation 构成，义为「想象力、想象的事物」
加 -ary 构成，义为「虚构的、想象中的」
加 -ive 构成，义为「富有想象力的」
同根名词，义为「图像、形象」

senses.title: To form a mental picture
senses.titleCN: 想象：在脑中造出画面
senses.definition: to form a picture of something in your mind
senses.definitionCN: 在脑海中形成某物的画面
senses.example: Imagine the street without any cars and the noise simply disappears.
senses.exampleCN: 想象一下这条街上没有车，噪音就完全消失了。
senses.why: The Latin verb imaginari means to picture to oneself, and the English verb keeps that workshop sense.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词 imaginari 意为「为自己成像」，英语动词保留了这种「动手造像」的感觉。

senses.title: To suppose as a guess
senses.titleCN: 猜想：把某情况当作可能
senses.definition: to suppose or believe something without proof
senses.definitionCN: 在没有证据时假定某事
senses.example: I imagine she has already heard the news.
senses.exampleCN: 我猜她已经听到这个消息了。
