senses.why: A picture held without proof becomes a guess, and the verb quietly shifts from creating to assuming.
senses.whyCN: 没有证据而持有的一幅画就变成猜测，动词便从创造悄悄转向假定。

senses.title: To invent in the mind
senses.titleCN: 构思：在脑中造出新东西
senses.definition: to invent a story, plan or design in the mind
senses.definitionCN: 在脑中编出故事、计划或设计
senses.example: He imagined a lamp that folds into the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 他构想出一种能折进墙里的灯。
senses.why: Imagining as inventing is the same act aimed at something that does not yet exist.
senses.whyCN: 作为发明的想象是同一个动作，只是对准了尚未存在之物。

senses.title: To picture an experience
senses.titleCN: 设想经历：把某种处境放进自己身上
senses.definition: to picture yourself in a situation or feeling
senses.definitionCN: 把某种处境或感受放在自己身上来设想
senses.example: Try to imagine living without a phone for a month.
senses.exampleCN: 试着设想一个月不用手机地生活。
senses.why: The verb often asks the listener to step into the picture, which is why it is used in advice.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词常请听者走进画面，因此多用于劝告。

intro.en: Imagine comes from Latin imaginari, to picture to oneself, built on imago, a likeness.
intro.cn: imagine 来自拉丁语 imaginari「为自己成像」，建立在 imago「相似之物」之上。

items.en: Imago, a likeness or a mask, is the root of the family.
items.cn: imago 意为「相似之物、面具」，是这个词族的根。

items.en: Imaginari was a deponent verb meaning to picture or to fancy.
items.cn: imaginari 是异态动词，意为「成像、幻想」。

items.en: Old French carried the verb north as imaginer.
items.cn: 古法语把动词向北带去，作 imaginer。

items.en: English borrowed it for forming pictures in the mind.
items.cn: 英语借入后用于表示在心中造像。

items.en: In everyday speech the verb also came to mean suppose.
items.cn: 在日常口语里，这个动词又发展出「猜想」义。

note.en: The look-alike group is the imagin- verb family; the near-meaning group holds verbs of supposing and picturing.
note.cn: 形近组是 imagin- 动词族；近义组收表示设想与揣测的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for the power of picturing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「想象力」。

entries.definition: Existing only in the mind.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「虚构的、想象中的」。

entries.definition: Good at picturing new things.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「富有想象力的」。

entries.definition: A likeness or picture; the root in plain form.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「图像、形象」，词根的朴素形态。

entries.definition: To think something is likely, close to the guess sense.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「假定、猜想」，接近猜想义。

entries.definition: To picture a future state, more formal than imagine.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「设想、展望」，比 imagine 正式。

entries.definition: To form a clear picture deliberately, as in training.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「在脑中呈像」，多用于训练。

entries.definition: To create something new, the result of imagining.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「发明」，是想象的结果。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the picture sense, the guess sense and the common patterns with doing.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借画面义、猜想义以及接 doing 的常见句式。

normal.en: Imagine holds an image inside; the verb is the act of making one.
normal.cn: imagine 里藏着一个 image，动词就是造出这幅画的动作。

normal.en: Imagine doing is the pattern; the second verb never takes to.
normal.cn: imagine doing 是固定搭配，后面绝不加 to。

normal.en: Hard to imagine is the phrase used when words run out.
normal.cn: 话语不够用时，人们就说 hard to imagine。

normal.en: The -ine ending marks the verb, -ation marks its noun.
normal.cn: -ine 结尾标记动词，-ation 结尾标记它的名词。

normal.en: To imagine a person is to lend them a stage in your head.
normal.cn: 想象一个人，就是在他脑中给他搭一个台子。

abstract.en: The verb is a projector: it throws a picture onto a wall that is not there yet.
abstract.cn: 这个动词像投影仪：把画面投到还不在的那面墙上。

abstract.en: Guessing and inventing live inside the same verb, because both begin with a picture held in the mind.
abstract.cn: 猜想与构思住在同一个动词里，因为两者都从脑中一幅画开始。

abstract.en: When someone says imagine, they are asking you to stand where they stand for a moment.
abstract.cn: 有人说 imagine，就是请你暂时站到他的位置上看一眼。

examples.en: Imagine a room with no windows and only one door.
examples.cn: 想象一个没有窗、只有一扇门的房间。

examples.en: I imagine he will arrive before noon.
examples.cn: 我猜他会在中午前到。

examples.en: She could not imagine working in a noisy office.
examples.cn: 她无法想象在嘈杂的办公室里工作。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一买鸡呢」——买鸡之前先在脑中想一遍怎么做

root: 拉丁语 imaginari（在心中描绘）经古法语 imaginer 进入英语，词根为 imago（相似之物）；同族词有 image、imagination、imaginary、imaginative。

sensesIntro.en: Imagine runs from making a picture, to guessing, to inventing, to stepping into another situation.
sensesIntro.cn: imagine 从造出画面，走到猜想、构思，再到把某种处境放进自己身上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: eyes closed by a window, already standing in tomorrow.
core.cn: 核心意象：在窗边闭上眼，人已经站到了明天。

branches.en: PICTURE LINE: the mind draws what the eye cannot see.
branches.cn: 画面线：心画出眼睛看不见的东西。

branches.en: GUESS LINE: the picture is held without proof.
branches.cn: 猜想线：这幅画没有证据支撑。

branches.en: INVENT LINE: the picture becomes a plan or a story.
branches.cn: 构思线：画面变成计划或故事。

branches.en: EMPATHY LINE: the listener is asked to step inside.
branches.cn: 共情线：请听者走进画里。

branches.en: CONTRAST: remember looks back, imagine looks forward.
branches.cn: 对照线：remember 向后看，imagine 向前看。

intro.en: One root of likeness and a verb ending, with the noun endings waiting one step away.
intro.cn: 一个表示相似的词根加动词词尾，名词词尾就在下一步等着。

latinIntro.en: Imago, imaginis supplies the root, and Latin added -inari to make the verb.
latinIntro.cn: imago, imaginis 提供词根，拉丁语加 -inari 造出动词。

items.example: It is the heart of the verb.
It is the noun without verb endings.
items.exampleCN: 它是没有动词词尾的同根名词。

definition_zh: 立即的；直接的；紧邻的；目前的
definition_en: happening at once, or with nothing in between
core_image: 手刚按下按钮，灯在同一瞬亮起
scene: 开关一响，屋里的灯亮起来，中间没有一丝停顿。The medicine gave immediate relief from the pain.
sceneCN: 这里 immediate 是「立即的」（第 1 个义项：没有时间间隔）；句意为这药立刻缓解了疼痛。按下按钮就亮的灯，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 形容词：立即的；直接的；紧邻的；当前的

derivatives.zh: 加 -ly 构成，义为「立即；直接地」
加 -acy 构成，义为「直接性、即时感」
去掉否定前缀 in- 后的词，义为「调解、居中」

senses.title: Happening at once
senses.titleCN: 立即的：中间没有时间间隔
senses.definition: happening or done at once, without delay
senses.definitionCN: 立刻发生或完成，没有耽搁
senses.example: The medicine gave immediate relief from the pain.
senses.exampleCN: 这药立刻缓解了疼痛。
senses.why: Latin in- here is not a denial but a negation of a gap: no middle step, so no waiting.
senses.whyCN: 这里拉丁语的 in- 不是否定事物，而是否定中间那一段：没有中间的步骤，所以不用等。

senses.title: Direct, with nothing between
senses.titleCN: 直接的：中间没有中介
senses.definition: direct, with no one and nothing in between
senses.definitionCN: 直接的，中间没有人或物隔着
senses.example: The storm was the immediate cause of the accident.
senses.exampleCN: 这场暴风雨是事故的直接原因。
senses.why: The same missing middle moves from time to cause: no step between cause and effect.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「缺了中间」从时间用到因果：因与果之间没有环节。

senses.title: Next to something
senses.titleCN: 紧邻的：在地理上挨着
senses.definition: nearest in space, close by without distance
senses.definitionCN: 在空间上最近，紧挨着而没有距离
senses.example: The school serves the immediate neighbourhood.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校服务邻近一带。
senses.why: Space repeats the logic of time: nothing between this place and the next.
senses.whyCN: 空间重复了时间的逻辑：此处与彼处之间什么也没有。

senses.title: Closest in relationship
senses.titleCN: 最亲的：关系上最近
senses.definition: closest in family or duty
senses.definitionCN: 在家庭或职责关系上最近的
senses.example: Only the immediate family was told the news first.
senses.exampleCN: 只有直系亲属先得到了消息。
senses.why: Family maps onto distance: the nearest circle is the one with no ring between.
senses.whyCN: 亲属关系被映射为距离：最近的那一圈，中间没有任何一环。

intro.en: Immediate is Latin in-, not, plus mediare, to be in the middle: literally with no middle.
intro.cn: immediate 是拉丁语 in-（不）加 mediare（处在中间）：字面上就是「没有中间」。

items.en: Medius meant middle and gave medium, mediate and median.
items.cn: medius 意为「中间的」，衍生出 medium、mediate、median。

items.en: Late Latin immediatus described things with nothing between them.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 immediatus 描述中间空无一物的事物。

items.en: French carried the adjective into English in the medieval period.
items.cn: 中古时期法语把这个形容词带入英语。

items.en: English first used it for what happens without delay.
items.cn: 英语最初用它指不耽搁就发生的事。

items.en: The same word then covered near places, near kin and direct causes.
items.cn: 此后同一个词也覆盖邻近地点、近亲与直接原因。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the medi- middle root; the near-meaning group holds words of speed and directness.
note.cn: 形近组共用 medi-「中间」词根；近义组收表示迅速与直接的词。

entries.definition: The adverb: at once, or directly.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「立即、直接地」。

entries.definition: The quality of being direct and unmediated.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「直接性、即时感」。

entries.definition: To act as a middle party between two sides.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「调解」，带 medi- 词根而无否定前缀。

entries.definition: A middle channel or average; root in plain form.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「媒介、中值」，词根的朴素形态。

entries.definition: Happening in a single moment, even faster than immediate.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「瞬间的」，比 immediate 更快。

entries.definition: Quick and without delay, often of a reply or action.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「及时的」，多指回复或行动。

entries.definition: With no middle person or step; close to the second sense.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「直接的」，接近第二义项。

entries.definition: Needing action now, stressing need rather than speed.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「紧急的」，强调需要而非速度。

normalIntro.en: The hooks work on the in- plus medi- build and on the family and cause collocations.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子围绕 in- 加 medi- 的构造以及直系亲属、直接原因等搭配。

normal.en: In- plus mediate means no mediation: nothing stands in the middle.
normal.cn: in- 加 mediate 意为「没有中介」：中间什么都没有。

normal.en: Immediate family are the people between you and everyone else.
normal.cn: immediate family 是站在你和别人之间的那圈人。

normal.en: An immediate reply gives the other person no waiting room.
normal.cn: immediate reply 让对方没有等待的余地。

normal.en: Immediately is the adverb and keeps the same promise of no gap.
normal.cn: 副词 immediately 同样承诺中间没有空隙。

normal.en: The immediate cause is the latest link before the effect.
normal.cn: immediate cause 是效果之前最近的那一环。

abstract.en: Think of a wire with no switch: press and it is already lit.
abstract.cn: 想象一根没有开关的导线：一按就已经亮了。

abstract.en: The same missing middle serves time, space, family and logic, which is why one adjective covers so much.
abstract.cn: 同一个「缺了中间」服务于时间、空间、亲缘和逻辑，于是一个形容词能覆盖这么多。

abstract.en: Immediacy is not speed only, it is the absence of anything to pass through.
abstract.cn: 「即时」不只是快，更是中间没有任何东西需要穿过。

examples.en: The order called for immediate action from the crew.
examples.cn: 这道命令要求机组立即行动。

examples.en: There was no immediate answer to the question.
examples.cn: 这个问题没有立刻得到答复。

examples.en: The hotel is in the immediate area of the station.
examples.cn: 这家旅馆就在车站附近。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一米的特」——一米的特快，说到就到

root: 拉丁语 immediatus，由否定前缀 in-（不）+ mediare（处在中间）构成，字面为「没有中间」；同族词有 immediately、immediacy、mediate、medium。

sensesIntro.en: Immediate always means no middle: in time no delay, in cause no step, in space nothing between, in family no ring around.
sensesIntro.cn: immediate 始终表示「中间空着」：时间上不耽搁，因果上无环节，空间上不隔物，亲属上不绕圈。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a button pressed and a lamp already on.
core.cn: 核心意象：按钮刚按下，灯已经亮了。

branches.en: TIME LINE: no delay between act and result.
branches.cn: 时间线：动作与结果之间没有延迟。

branches.en: CAUSE LINE: no step between cause and effect.
branches.cn: 因果线：因与果之间没有环节。

branches.en: SPACE LINE: no distance to the neighbouring place.
branches.cn: 空间线：到邻近之处没有距离。

branches.en: FAMILY LINE: no ring of relatives in between.
branches.cn: 亲属线：中间没有别的亲戚环绕。

branches.en: CONTRAST: delayed and indirect both put a middle back in.
branches.cn: 对照线：delayed 与 indirect 等于把「中间」放回去。

intro.en: A negative prefix that denies a gap, a middle root, and an adjective ending.
intro.cn: 一个否定存在间隙的前缀、一个表示「中间」的词根，再加形容词词尾。

latinIntro.en: In- denies, medius supplies the middle, and the Latin participle ending closes it.
latinIntro.cn: in- 否定，medius 提供「中间」，拉丁分词词尾收住这个词。

items.exampleCN: 它同样出现在 medium 里。
它是正面词形的孪生词。

definition_zh: 立即；马上；直接地；紧挨着
definition_en: at once, without delay; or directly, with nothing between
core_image: 话刚落，对方已经站起身往外走
scene: 警报刚响，走廊里的人全都在同一秒转向安全门。She recognised him immediately and dropped the bag.
sceneCN: 这里 immediately 是「立即、马上」（第 1 个义项：没有耽搁）；句意是她立刻认出了他，手里的包掉了下来。警报响后一秒转向的人们，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 副词：立即、马上；直接地；紧挨着
连词（英式）：一……就……

derivatives.zh: 去掉 -ly 得到的形容词，义为「立即的、直接的」
同根名词，义为「直接性、即时感」
去掉否定前缀后的同根词，义为「调解」

senses.title: At once
senses.titleCN: 立即：没有任何耽搁
senses.definition: without any delay, at this very moment
senses.definitionCN: 没有任何耽搁，就在此刻
senses.example: She recognised him immediately and dropped the bag.
senses.exampleCN: 她立刻认出了他，手里的包掉了下来。
senses.why: The adverb -ly says how: with the middle removed, so nothing stands between the moment and the act.
senses.whyCN: 副词 -ly 交代方式：把中间去掉，于是时刻与行动之间什么都不留。

senses.title: Directly, with nothing between
senses.titleCN: 直接地：中间没有中介
senses.definition: directly, with no person or thing in between
senses.definitionCN: 直接地，中间没有人或物
senses.example: The order came immediately from the director.
senses.exampleCN: 这道命令直接来自主管。
senses.why: Time becomes relation: no go-between means the same missing middle.
senses.whyCN: 时间变成关系：没有中间传话的人，仍是同一种「缺了中间」。

senses.title: Right next to
senses.titleCN: 紧挨着：在地点上紧贴
senses.definition: directly beside, with no space or object between
senses.definitionCN: 紧贴旁边，中间没有空隙或别的物体
senses.example: The bag was standing immediately behind the door.
senses.exampleCN: 那只包就立在门后紧挨着的地方。
senses.why: Distance works like time: no space, no go-between, the adverb simply names the absence of anything in the middle.
senses.whyCN: 距离与时间同理：没有空隙、没有中介，副词只是命名「中间空无一物」。

senses.title: As soon as
senses.titleCN: 一……就：引导时间状语
senses.definition: as soon as, introducing a clause as a conjunction
senses.definitionCN: 作为连词引导从句，表示「一……就……」
senses.example: Immediately the bell rang, the hall fell silent.
senses.exampleCN: 铃一响，大厅就静了下来。
senses.why: The older sense of no gap turned into a linker for two events that touch.
senses.whyCN: 「没有空隙」的旧义，化成了连接两个紧挨着的事件的连词。

intro.en: Immediately is the adjective immediate plus the English adverb ending -ly.
intro.cn: immediately 是形容词 immediate 加上英语副词词尾 -ly。

items.en: Medius, middle, is the root behind the whole family.
items.cn: medius「中间」是整个词族的根。

items.en: Immediatus meant with nothing in between.
items.cn: immediatus 意为「中间没有任何东西」。

items.en: French handed the adjective to English in the medieval period.
items.cn: 中古时期法语把这个形容词交给英语。

items.en: English kept it for acts done without delay.
items.cn: 英语用它指不耽搁就完成的动作。

items.en: Adding -ly produced the adverb and, in British use, a conjunction.
items.cn: 加上 -ly 造出副词，并在英式用法里成了连词。

note.en: The look-alike group is the immedi- adverb family; the near-meaning group holds adverbs of speed.
note.cn: 形近组是 immedi- 副词族；近义组收表示迅速与直接的副词。

entries.definition: The adjective the adverb is built on.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，副词的基础。

entries.definition: The quality of having nothing in between.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「直接性、即时感」。

entries.definition: To stand in the middle as a go-between.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「居于中间调解」。

entries.definition: A middle channel; root without prefixes.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「媒介」，无前缀的词根形态。

entries.definition: The plain phrase for without delay.
entries.definitionCN: 短语，义为「立刻」，最普通的说法。

entries.definition: In an instant; even sharper and more literary.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「瞬间地」，更锐利也更书面。

entries.definition: Without delay and usually on time, often of duties.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「及时地」，多指按时的行动。

entries.definition: With no go-between; matches the second sense.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「直接地」，对应第二义项。

normalIntro.en: The hooks rely on the -ly ending, the British conjunction use and the after and behind pairs.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子依靠 -ly 词尾、英式连词用法以及 after 与 behind 等搭配。

normal.en: Immediately is immediate wearing -ly, so it describes the timing of an act.
normal.cn: immediately 就是 immediate 披上 -ly，描述动作的时机。

normal.en: British speakers can begin a sentence with it: Immediately the bell rang.
normal.cn: 英式用法可以把它放在句首：Immediately the bell rang.

normal.en: Immediately after and immediately before pin down a point on a timeline.
normal.cn: immediately after 与 immediately before 把时间点钉得很准。

normal.en: The in- takes away the middle, the -ly says this is how it happened.
normal.cn: in- 拿掉中间，-ly 说明事情就是这样发生的。

normal.en: Say it and it is already done: that is the whole promise of the word.
normal.cn: 话说出口，事已经做完：这就是这个词的全部承诺。

abstract.en: This adverb is a stopwatch that reads zero.
abstract.cn: 这个副词是一块读数为零的秒表。

abstract.en: It removes not the action but the waiting, and waiting is what the listener cares about.
abstract.cn: 它去掉的不是动作，而是等待，而等待正是听者所在意的。

abstract.en: Used of a person, it means there is nobody standing between you and them.
abstract.cn: 用在人身上时，它表示你与对方之间没有别人站着。

examples.en: Call the doctor immediately if the fever rises.
examples.cn: 如果体温升高，立刻叫医生。

examples.en: The reply came immediately from the head office.
examples.cn: 回信直接来自总部。

examples.en: There is a small car park immediately next to the hall.
examples.cn: 大厅紧旁边有一个小车场。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一米的特离」——一米的特快列车离开，秒到

root: 形容词 immediate（拉丁语 immediatus＝in-「不」+ mediare「处在中间」）加副词词尾 -ly；同族词有 immediate、immediacy、mediate、medium。

sensesIntro.en: Immediately covers no delay in time, no go-between in relation, no gap in space, and even a clause linker.
sensesIntro.cn: immediately 覆盖时间上无耽搁、关系上无中介、空间上无间隙，甚至可作连词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: words barely finished and the other person already walking out.
core.cn: 核心意象：话刚说完，对方已经走出去。

branches.en: TIME LINE: nothing waits between word and deed.
branches.cn: 时间线：言语与行动之间没有等待。

branches.en: RELATION LINE: nothing stands between you and the source.
branches.cn: 关系线：你与来源之间不隔人或物。

branches.en: SPACE LINE: nothing sits between the two things.
branches.cn: 空间线：两物之间不隔东西。

branches.en: LINK LINE: two events touch with no gap of time.
branches.cn: 连接线：两个事件紧贴，中间没有时间空隙。

branches.en: CONTRAST: eventually is the same act with the wait put back.
branches.cn: 对照线：eventually 把等待又放回去。

intro.en: The negative of a middle root, closed by a Latin ending and then an English -ly.
intro.cn: 「中间」词根的否定式，加拉丁词尾、再加英语 -ly 收束。

latinIntro.en: In- denies, medius gives the middle, and the family reaches English through French.
latinIntro.cn: in- 否定，medius 给出「中间」，词族经法语进入英语。

definition_zh: 暗示；意味着；含……的意思；含有……的必要条件
definition_en: to suggest something without saying it openly
core_image: 话里只说了一半，另一半藏在桌下
scene: 面试官合上材料，只说了一句「我们会尽快通知」，桌上那只表却已经停了。A blank tax return implies that nothing was earned.
sceneCN: 这里 imply 是「暗示、意味着」（第 1 个义项：话里含有而未明说）；句意为一份空白的报税单意味着没有任何收入。话里藏着的那另一半，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 动词：暗示、意味着；含有……的意思

derivatives.zh: 加 -ation 构成，义为「含义、暗示、牵连」
同根形容词，义为「含蓄的、不言明的」
过去分词作形容词，义为「隐含的」

senses.title: To hint without saying
senses.titleCN: 暗示：不直说而让人领会
senses.definition: to suggest something indirectly, without stating it
senses.definitionCN: 不直接说出而使人领会某事
senses.example: Her silence implied that she disagreed.
senses.exampleCN: 她的沉默暗示她并不同意。
senses.why: Latin implicare means to fold in; what is implied is folded inside the sentence, not laid out on it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 implicare 意为「折进去」；被暗示的内容折在句子里面，而不摊在句子表面。

senses.title: To mean as a consequence
senses.titleCN: 意味着：作为必然结果而含有
senses.definition: to mean something as a necessary result
senses.definitionCN: 作为必然结果而含有某层意思
senses.example: A licence implies that the holder has passed the test.
senses.exampleCN: 有执照就意味着持照人通过了考试。
senses.why: The folded-in content can be a logical consequence, and then implying is close to entailing.
senses.whyCN: 折进去的内容也可以是逻辑后果，此时暗示便接近「必然含有」。

senses.title: To bring along by necessity
senses.titleCN: 必然带来：含有必要条件
senses.definition: to involve something as a necessary condition
senses.definitionCN: 把某事作为必要条件一并包含
senses.example: A long stay implies a steady income.
senses.exampleCN: 长期停留必然意味着有稳定的收入。
senses.why: Conditions travel with actions; the verb records what cannot be left behind.
senses.whyCN: 条件跟着行动一起走，这个动词记下那些无法被落下的事物。

senses.title: To indicate without words
senses.titleCN: 表明：由迹象而不由言语表示
senses.definition: to be a sign of something without any statement
senses.definitionCN: 不以言语而以迹象表示某事
senses.example: The empty shelves implied a shortage of paper.
senses.exampleCN: 空空的货架表明纸张短缺。
senses.why: Things can imply as well as people; a sign folds its meaning into itself too.
senses.whyCN: 事物也能暗示，不限于人；一个迹象同样把意义折在自己的里面。

intro.en: Imply comes from Latin implicare, to fold in, from in- plus plicare, to fold.
intro.cn: imply 来自拉丁语 implicare「折进去」，由 in- 加 plicare「折叠」组成。

items.en: Plicare meant to fold, and it also underlies complicated and explicit.
items.cn: plicare 意为「折叠」，也是 complicated 与 explicit 的底层词根。

items.en: Implicare meant to involve or entangle, to fold something into something else.
items.cn: implicare 意为「缠绕、使牵连」，即把一物折进另一物。

items.en: Old French emplier carried the sense of involving or entangling.
items.cn: 古法语 emplier 带有「牵连」之意。

items.en: English used imply first for entangling and then for meaning indirectly.
items.cn: 英语起初用 imply 表示牵连，后来才指间接含有。

items.en: In logic and law the verb also marks what follows of necessity.
items.cn: 在逻辑与法律中，这个动词也标记必然推出之事。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the plic- fold root or the im- prefix; the near-meaning group holds words of suggesting.
note.cn: 形近组共用 plic-「折叠」词根或 im- 前缀；近义组收表示暗示的词。

entries.definition: What is implied, or a possible consequence.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「含义、牵连」。

entries.definition: Folded in and unstated, the adjective of the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「含蓄的、不言明的」。

entries.definition: Folded out and stated openly, the direct opposite.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「明确的」，与 implicit 相反。

entries.definition: To put to use; the ending is shared, the root differs.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「应用」，词尾相同而词根不同。

entries.definition: To put an idea gently into another mind.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「提示、建议」，最接近的日常词。

entries.definition: To point at something lightly, even less direct than imply.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「暗示」，比 imply 更轻。

entries.definition: To show by signs, close to the fourth sense.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「表明、指示」，接近第四义项。

entries.definition: The plain verb for carrying a meaning, stated or not.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「意思是」，最朴素的对应词。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the fold-in root, the implied adjective and the logic sense.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借「折进去」的词根、implied 这个形容词以及逻辑用法。

normal.en: Imply has the same fold as complicated: meaning folded into the sentence.
normal.cn: imply 与 complicated 共用「折」：意义折进了句子里。

normal.en: Implicit is the adjective, implication is the noun, imply is the act.
normal.cn: implicit 是形容词，implication 是名词，imply 是那个动作。

normal.en: Her silence implied disagreement is the standard example sentence.
normal.cn: Her silence implied disagreement 是标准的例句。

normal.en: Implied terms are what a contract holds without spelling out.
normal.cn: implied terms 是合同里没写出来却含有的条款。

normal.en: Imply points at the meaning, the listener has to unfold it.
normal.cn: imply 指着那个意思，需要听者自己去展开。

abstract.en: Picture a folded letter: the words are inside, and you are told only that something is written.
abstract.cn: 想象一封折好的信：字句在里面，你只被告知里面写了东西。

abstract.en: Two minds share the work: one folds, the other unfolds, and the word names only the folding.
abstract.cn: 两个头脑分担了工作：一个折，一个展，而这个词只命名了折叠。

abstract.en: A sign implies without speaking, which is why the word covers objects and silence as well as speech.
abstract.cn: 迹象不发一言就能暗示，因此这个词也覆盖物件与沉默。

examples.en: The wording implied that the offer could be withdrawn.
examples.cn: 这一措辞意味着这个报价可能被撤回。

examples.en: A sudden change of plan implies that something went wrong.
examples.cn: 计划突然改变意味着哪里出了问题。

examples.en: Are you implying that I was careless?
examples.cn: 你是在暗示我不小心吗？

dict_mnemonic.text: 「隐普来」——隐隐地普（通）遍传来一句，没明说

root: 拉丁语 implicare（折进去、缠绕），由 in-（向内）+ plicare（折叠）构成；同族词有 implication、implicit、explicit、complicate。

sensesIntro.en: To imply is to fold meaning inside a sentence, a condition or a sign, so the other side must unfold it.
sensesIntro.cn: imply 是把意义折进句子、条件或迹象里，需要对方去展开。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: half a sentence spoken and the other half left folded underneath.
core.cn: 核心意象：话说出一半，另一半折在下面。

branches.en: WORD LINE: the hint sits inside what was said.
branches.cn: 话语线：暗示藏在说出口的话里。

branches.en: LOGIC LINE: the meaning follows of necessity.
branches.cn: 逻辑线：意义作为必然结果随之而来。

branches.en: CONDITION LINE: the action brings requirements along.
branches.cn: 条件线：行动把前提一并带来。

branches.en: SIGN LINE: the shelves speak without words.
branches.cn: 迹象线：货架不用言语就说了话。

branches.en: CONTRAST: state means stated, imply means folded in and unsaid.
branches.cn: 对照线：stated 是明说，implied 是折进去而没说。

intro.en: An inward prefix on a Latin root meaning to fold, plus a French verb ending.
intro.cn: 一个表示「向内」的前缀加拉丁词根「折叠」，再加法语动词词尾。

latinIntro.en: In- plus plicare, to fold, gives implicare, the ancestor of the English verb.
latinIntro.cn: in- 加 plicare「折叠」得到 implicare，是英语动词的祖先。

items.exampleCN: 它也出现在 complicated 里。
它保留了词根的可见性。

definition_zh: 强加；施加（税收、惩罚）；征收；勉强麻烦（某人）
definition_en: to force something on someone by authority
core_image: 一只手把印章用力压在文件上，留下无法抹去的痕迹
scene: 边境口岸的窗口还没开，队尾已经开始抱怨这项新规定。The city imposed a heavy tax on vacant buildings.
sceneCN: 这里 impose 是「征收、强制施加」（第 1 个义项：凭借权力加于人）；句意为这座城市对空置建筑征收重税。那只压在文件上的印章，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 动词：强加；征收（税等）；处以（惩罚）；勉强麻烦

derivatives.zh: 加 -ition 构成，义为「强加、征收、负担」
现在分词作形容词，义为「壮观的、气势逼人的」
过去分词作形容词，义为「强制施加的」

senses.title: To force a rule or tax
senses.titleCN: 强加：凭借权力加诸于人
senses.definition: to officially force a rule, tax or punishment on people
senses.definitionCN: 以官方权力把规则、税负或惩罚加在人们身上
senses.example: The city imposed a heavy tax on vacant buildings.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市对空置建筑征收重税。
senses.why: Latin in- plus ponere, to place, gives impose: to place something onto somebody, whether or not they want it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 in- 加 ponere「放置」得到 impose：把东西放到别人身上，不管对方愿不愿意。

senses.title: To burden someone
senses.titleCN: 使人承担：让人承受额外负担
senses.definition: to make someone carry a burden, often unfairly
senses.definitionCN: 使人承担通常并不公平的负担
senses.example: The new deadline imposed a long weekend of work on the team.
senses.exampleCN: 新的截止期让团队整个周末都在加班。
senses.why: The same placing becomes a load when the person placed upon has no say.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「放置」压到无权发言的人身上，就成了一种负担。

senses.title: To take advantage of
senses.titleCN: 占便宜：勉强别人、不当占用
senses.definition: to expect too much from someone or to use them unfairly
senses.definitionCN: 对别人要求过分，或不当占用他人
senses.example: I hope I am not imposing on your kindness.
senses.exampleCN: 希望我这不是在占你的便宜。
senses.why: When there is no authority behind the placing, the verb softens into an apology for one more request.
senses.whyCN: 当「放置」背后没有权力时，这个动词便软化成对多提要求的致歉。

senses.title: To set a condition
senses.titleCN: 强加条件：要求对方必须先满足
senses.definition: to state a condition that must be accepted
senses.definitionCN: 提出必须被接受的条件
senses.example: The lender imposed strict conditions on the loan.
senses.exampleCN: 贷款方对这笔贷款施加了严格条件。
senses.why: A condition placed on an agreement is the abstract form of the same weight.
senses.whyCN: 加在协议上的条件，是同一份重量在抽象层面的形态。

intro.en: Impose is Latin in-, onto, plus ponere, to place: to place a burden onto someone.
intro.cn: impose 是拉丁语 in-（到……之上）加 ponere（放置）：把负担放到别人身上。

items.en: Ponere meant to put or place, and it also stands behind compose and deposit.
items.cn: ponere 意为「放置」，也是 compose 与 deposit 的词根。

items.en: Imponere meant to put upon, to lay on, and also to cheat by placing something false.
items.cn: imponere 意为「放到上面、加于」，也可指以假物欺骗。

items.en: Old French imposer kept the placing sense and added authority.
items.cn: 古法语 imposer 保留「放置」之意，并带上权力色彩。

items.en: English took the verb for taxing and ruling by authority.
items.cn: 英语借入这个动词，用于凭权力征税与下命令。

items.en: A softer use then appeared for troubling people with requests.
items.cn: 此后出现较软的用法，指以请求去麻烦别人。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the pos- place root; the near-meaning group holds verbs of forcing.
note.cn: 形近组共用 pos-「放置」词根；近义组收表示强制的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for an unwanted burden or a tax.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「强加、征收、负担」。

entries.definition: Grand and impressive to look at, a separate sense.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「气势逼人的」，是独立义项。

entries.definition: To put things together; shares the place root.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「组成」，共用「放置」词根。

entries.definition: To put out in the open; same root, different prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使暴露」，同词根不同前缀。

entries.definition: To make a rule obeyed; the effect of imposing it.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「执行」，是 impose 的结果。

entries.definition: The plain verb for making someone do something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「强迫」，最朴素的说法。

entries.definition: To raise a tax officially, close to the first sense.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「征收（税）」，接近第一义项。

entries.definition: To load someone with weight, close to the second sense.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使负担」，接近第二义项。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the place root, the tax collocations and the polite apology use.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借「放置」词根、征税搭配以及客气的致歉用法。

normal.en: Impose is in plus pose, putting something onto a person.
normal.cn: impose 是 in 加 pose，把东西放到人身上。

normal.en: Impose a tax, impose a ban, impose a fine: three official phrases.
normal.cn: impose a tax、impose a ban、impose a fine 是三个官方短语。

normal.en: 「I hope I am not imposing」 is the polite way to ask a favour.
normal.cn: 「I hope I am not imposing」是请人帮忙时的客气话。

normal.en: Impose and expose differ by one prefix: one puts on, one puts out.
normal.cn: impose 与 expose 只差一个前缀：一个放上去，一个放出来。

normal.en: An imposed rule comes from above and lands on the rest of us.
normal.cn: 被 imposed 的规则自上而下，落到其他人头上。

abstract.en: Picture a seal pressed onto a document: heavy, official, and impossible to argue with.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚印章压到文件上：沉重、官方，无从争辩。

abstract.en: The same weight can be a law, a bill or a favour asked too often, and one verb covers all three.
abstract.cn: 同一份重量可以是法律、账单，也可以是求得太多的帮忙，一个动词涵盖三者。

abstract.en: Authority is the hidden part of the word: without it, placing things on others becomes mere impoliteness.
abstract.cn: 权力是这个词藏起来的部分：没有它，把东西放到别人身上就只是失礼。

examples.en: The government imposed a ban on single-use plastics.
examples.cn: 政府实施了对一次性塑料的禁令。

examples.en: Do not let the schedule impose on your health.
examples.cn: 别让日程安排损害你的健康。

examples.en: Heavy fines were imposed on drivers who ignored the sign.
examples.cn: 无视标志的司机被处以重罚。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「硬破子」——硬把一个破担子压到你身上

root: 拉丁语 imponere（放到上面），由 in-（向上、向内）+ ponere（放置）构成，经法语 imposer 进入英语；同族词有 imposition、imposing、compose、expose。

sensesIntro.en: Impose places something onto someone: a law, a burden, a condition, or just one more favour.
sensesIntro.cn: impose 是把东西放上去：法律、负担、条件，或者只是一个多余的请求。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a seal pressed hard onto paper, leaving a mark that cannot be argued away.
core.cn: 核心意象：印章重重压在纸上，留下无法辩驳的痕。

branches.en: LAW LINE: the state places a tax or a rule.
branches.cn: 法律线：国家放上税负或规则。

branches.en: LOAD LINE: the weight lands on people or terms.
branches.cn: 负担线：重量落在人身上或条款里。

branches.en: MANNER LINE: without authority the placing becomes a favour.
branches.cn: 礼貌线：没有权力时，放置变成了请求。

branches.en: COST LINE: someone pays for what another decided.
branches.cn: 代价线：一人决定，另一人付出。

branches.en: CONTRAST: offer invites, impose presses.
branches.cn: 对照线：offer 是邀请，impose 是压上。

intro.en: An inward prefix plus the Latin verb for placing, carried into English through French.
intro.cn: 一个表示「向上、向内」的前缀加拉丁语「放置」动词，经法语进入英语。

latinIntro.en: In- plus ponere gives imponere; the French ending reshaped the English form.
latinIntro.cn: in- 加 ponere 得到 imponere，法语词尾又重塑了英语形式。

items.example: It marks the direction of the placing.

items.exampleCN: 它也出现在 compose 里。

definition_zh: 给……留下深刻印象；使钦佩；使铭记；压印
definition_en: to make someone feel admiration, or to fix something in the mind
core_image: 一枚印章按进软蜡，印迹留了下来
scene: 招聘官看完那份作品集，往后靠在椅背上看了很久。Her quiet confidence impressed the whole committee.
sceneCN: 这里 impress 是「给……留下深刻印象」（第 1 个义项：使人心生敬意）；句意为她沉静而自信的样子给整个委员会留下了深刻印象。按进软蜡的那枚印章，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 动词：给……留下深刻印象；使铭记；压印
名词（较少用）：印记、印象

collocations.zh: 向某人强调、使某人铭记

derivatives.zh: 加 -ion 构成，义为「印象、印记」
加 -ive 构成，义为「令人印象深刻的」
过去分词作形容词，义为「印象深刻的」

senses.title: To make a strong impression
senses.titleCN: 使留下深刻印象：令人钦佩
senses.definition: to cause someone to feel admiration or respect
senses.definitionCN: 使人产生敬佩或赞叹之感
senses.example: Her quiet confidence impressed the whole committee.
senses.exampleCN: 她沉静而自信的样子给整个委员会留下了深刻印象。
senses.why: Latin imprimere means to press into; admiration is the print a person leaves on your mind.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 imprimere 意为「压进去」；敬佩正是一个人留在你心上的印迹。

senses.title: To fix an idea in the mind
senses.titleCN: 使铭记：把某个道理印进心里
senses.definition: to make someone remember an idea or a rule firmly
senses.definitionCN: 让人牢牢记住所讲的道理或规矩
senses.example: The teacher impressed on us the need for careful notes.
senses.exampleCN: 老师反复叮嘱我们做笔记要细心。
senses.why: The physical print is applied to belief: what is pressed in is not ink but a lesson.
senses.whyCN: 具体的印迹被用到信念上：压进去的不是墨，而是一课道理。

senses.title: To press a mark into a surface
senses.titleCN: 压印：在物体表面留下痕迹
senses.definition: to press a shape or pattern into a material
senses.definitionCN: 把形状或图样压进某种材料
senses.example: The seal was impressed into hot wax.
senses.exampleCN: 印章被压进滚热的封蜡里。
senses.why: This is the oldest and most literal layer of the word, and the source of all the others.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词最古老、最字面的一层，也是其余义项的来源。

senses.title: To be memorable
senses.titleCN: 令人记住：留下难以忘记的样子
senses.definition: to stand out in someone's memory in a lasting way
senses.definitionCN: 在某人记忆中留下持久而鲜明的样子
senses.example: The first lines of the speech impressed themselves on everyone present.
senses.exampleCN: 演讲开头的几句话刻在了在场每个人心里。
senses.why: The mind takes the place of the wax, so an idea can print itself and stay.
senses.whyCN: 心取代了蜡的位置，于是想法可以自行印上去并留下来。

intro.en: Impress is Latin in- plus premere, to press: to press a mark into something.
intro.cn: impress 是拉丁语 in- 加 premere「压」：把印痕压进某物。

items.en: Premere meant to press, and it also stands behind press and compress.
items.cn: premere 意为「压」，也是 press 与 compress 的词根。

items.en: Imprimere meant to press into, to stamp, and to print.
items.cn: imprimere 意为「压入、盖印、印刷」。

items.en: French empreindre kept the idea of a mark pressed onto a surface.
items.cn: 法语 empreindre 保留了「压到表面留痕」之意。

items.en: English used it for stamps and seals before using it for minds.
items.cn: 英语先用它指盖印，之后才用到人心上。

items.en: By the sixteenth century it also meant to affect someone deeply.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，它也表示深深打动某人。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the press- root; the near-meaning group holds verbs of affecting others.
note.cn: 形近组共用 press-「压」词根；近义组收表示打动他人的动词。

entries.definition: The mark left behind, or the feeling produced.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「印象、印记」。

entries.definition: Able to impress; describes the thing, not the viewer.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「令人印象深刻的」，修饰事物。

entries.definition: To push steadily on something; the root in plain form.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「按压」，词根的朴素形态。

entries.definition: To press out a meaning; shares the root, other prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「表达」，同词根不同前缀。

entries.definition: To change someone's thinking, without admiration implied.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「影响」，不含敬佩之意。

entries.definition: To make someone believe or agree, aims at consent.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「说服」，目标是让人同意。

entries.definition: The fixed pattern for fixing an idea in a mind.
entries.definitionCN: 固定搭配，把道理印进心里。

entries.definition: To fill someone with energy or awe, close in feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「激励、启发」，感受相近。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the seal-in-wax image, the -ssive adjective and the on pattern.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借印章入蜡的画面、-ssive 形容词以及 on 的搭配。

normal.en: Impress is press with in-: something is pressed into your mind.
normal.cn: impress 就是带 in- 的 press：有东西被压进你心里。

normal.en: The thing is impressive, you are impressed: the adjective and participle split the work.
normal.cn: 东西是 impressive，你是 impressed：形容词与分词分工清楚。

normal.en: Impress on someone is the phrase for a lesson not to be forgotten.
normal.cn: impress on someone 是「让人记住一课」的说法。

normal.en: Press, compress, express and impress all share one Latin verb.
normal.cn: press、compress、express、impress 共用同一个拉丁动词。

normal.en: Be impressed by is what you say after someone good has left the room.
normal.cn: be impressed by 是优秀的人离开房间后你会说的话。

abstract.en: A seal pressed in wax leaves a shape; a person pressed into your memory leaves a feeling.
abstract.cn: 印章压在蜡上留下形状；一个人压进你的记忆留下感受。

abstract.en: The oldest sense is physical and the newest is emotional, one verb with the same verb under both.
abstract.cn: 最老的义项是物理的，最新的义项是情感的，同一种压在其下。

abstract.en: Nobody can impress on purpose for long, which is why the word tends to describe what someone did without knowing.
abstract.cn: 没人能长久地刻意让人敬佩，因此这个词常用来描述某人无意中做到了的事。

examples.en: The design impressed the judges at once.
examples.cn: 这个设计立刻打动了评委。

examples.en: She impressed on the children the need to wash their hands.
examples.cn: 她叮嘱孩子们要洗手。

examples.en: The pattern was impressed into the leather with a hot tool.
examples.cn: 图案是用烧热的工具压进皮革里的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一姆普瑞斯」——一姆（拇）指按上去，留下印子

root: 拉丁语 imprimere（压入、盖印），由 in-（向内）+ premere（压）构成，经法语进入英语；同族词有 impression、impressive、press、express、compress。

sensesIntro.en: Impress begins with a seal in wax and ends with a person in your memory; the press never disappears.
sensesIntro.cn: impress 从蜡上的印章走到记忆里的人，那个「压」始终没消失。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a seal pressed into soft wax, the shape staying behind.
core.cn: 核心意象：印章压进软蜡，留下形状。

branches.en: ADMIRATION LINE: a person leaves a strong print.
branches.cn: 敬佩线：一个人留下深印。

branches.en: MEMORY LINE: a lesson or a look presses itself in.
branches.cn: 记忆线：一课道理或一个神情自己压了进去。

branches.en: MATERIAL LINE: the seal and the wax keep it physical.
branches.cn: 实物线：印章与蜡保留了物理义。

branches.en: AUDIENCE LINE: the print is felt by the observer.
branches.cn: 观众线：印痕由旁观者感受到。

branches.en: CONTRAST: paint stays on a surface, impress goes below it.
branches.cn: 对照线：颜料留在表面，impress 进到表面之下。

intro.en: An inward prefix and a Latin root of pressing, with the ordinary English verb endings.
intro.cn: 一个表示「向内」的前缀加拉丁语「压」词根，再配寻常的英语动词词尾。

latinIntro.en: In- and premere combine into imprimere, the ancestor of the English verb.
latinIntro.cn: in- 与 premere 合成 imprimere，是英语动词的祖先。

items.example: It shows the mark going below the surface.
items.exampleCN: 它表示印痕进入表面之下。

items.example: It names what is left behind.

definition_zh: 印象；看法；印记；压印；仿效
definition_en: the feeling or idea you get about someone or something
core_image: 蜡上留下的一枚清晰印痕，形状与印章分毫不差
scene: 第一次见面只有十分钟，走出电梯时她心里已经有了判断。The first impression on the visitors was one of order and calm.
sceneCN: 这里 impression 是「印象」（第 1 个义项：接触后形成的看法）；句意为访客的第一印象是秩序与平静。蜡上留下的那枚印痕，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 名词：印象、看法；印记、压印；仿效

derivatives.zh: 去掉 -ion 得到的动词，义为「给……留下印象、压印」
加 -ive 构成，义为「令人印象深刻的」
加 -ist 构成，义为「印象派画家」

senses.title: A feeling about someone
senses.titleCN: 印象：接触后形成的看法
senses.definition: the feeling or opinion you form about someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 接触某人或某物后形成的感受或看法
senses.example: The first impression on the visitors was one of order and calm.
senses.exampleCN: 访客的第一印象是秩序与平静。
senses.why: Latin impressio is a pressing in; an opinion is what a person pressed into your mind.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 impressio 意为「压入」；看法正是一个人压进你心里的东西。

senses.title: A mark pressed into a surface
senses.titleCN: 压痕：表面被压出的印记
senses.definition: a mark made by pressing one object into another
senses.definitionCN: 把一个物体压入另一物体所留下的痕迹
senses.example: You can still see the impression of the seal in the wax.
senses.exampleCN: 在蜡上还能看到印章压出的痕迹。
senses.why: This is the literal layer: the wax keeps the shape of what was pressed into it.
senses.whyCN: 这是字面的一层：蜡保留了压进去之物的形状。

senses.title: An imitation
senses.titleCN: 仿效：模仿他人的样子
senses.definition: a copy of another person's manner or voice, done to entertain
senses.definitionCN: 为逗乐而模仿他人的神态或声音
senses.example: He does a funny impression of the headmaster.
senses.exampleCN: 他模仿校长，模仿得很好笑。
senses.why: An imitation is a print taken from a person, so the same noun covers it.
senses.whyCN: 模仿就是取自某人的印样，因此同一个名词也能涵盖它。

senses.title: A single printing run
senses.titleCN: 印次：一次印刷的份数
senses.definition: all the copies of a book printed at one time
senses.definitionCN: 一次印刷出的全部书籍
senses.example: The book ran to five impressions in one year.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书一年内印了五次。
senses.why: Printing is pressing ink onto paper, and each run leaves one batch behind.
senses.whyCN: 印刷就是把墨压到纸上，每一次都留下一批成品。

intro.en: Impression is the Latin noun impressio, a pressing in, from imprimere, to press into.
intro.cn: impression 是拉丁名词 impressio「压入」，来自 imprimere「压进去」。

items.en: Premere, to press, gave the whole family its root.
items.cn: premere「压」给整个词族提供了词根。

items.en: Impressio meant a pressing, a stamp, or the image left by one.
items.cn: impressio 意为「按压、盖印」，或按压留下的图样。

items.en: French passed the noun into English with both the physical and mental senses.
items.cn: 法语把这个名词传入英语，兼有实物与心理两层意思。

items.en: English used it early for the effect left on a mind or a feeling.
items.cn: 英语很早就用它指留在心中或情绪上的效果。

items.en: The rise of printing added the sense of one complete print run.
items.cn: 印刷业的兴起又添上「一次完整印刷」的义项。

note.en: The look-alike group is the impress- word family; the near-meaning group holds words for views and marks.
note.cn: 形近组是 impress- 词族；近义组收表示看法与痕迹的词。

entries.definition: The verb from which the noun is formed.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，名词由它构成。

entries.definition: Causing admiration, said of the cause rather than the effect.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「令人印象深刻的」，说原因而非结果。

entries.definition: An artist of the school that trusts first impressions.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「印象派画家」。

entries.definition: A pressing out; shares the root, not the prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「表达」，同词根不同前缀。

entries.definition: The general word for what you sense; the plainest partner.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「感觉」，最普通的对应词。

entries.definition: A considered opinion; close to the opinion sense.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「看法」，接近看法一义。

entries.definition: A visible trace; close to the literal sense.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「痕迹」，接近字面义。

entries.definition: The picture others carry, close to the reputation side.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「形象」，接近名声的一面。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the wax mark, the first impression phrase and the under the impression idiom.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借蜡上印痕、first impression 短语以及 under the impression 这一习语。

normal.en: Impression is the print that impress leaves behind.
normal.cn: impression 就是 impress 留下的那个印。

normal.en: First impressions are what everyone claims never to trust.
normal.cn: first impressions 是人人声称从不相信的东西。

normal.en: Under the impression that means believing wrongly.
normal.cn: under the impression that 意为「误以为」。

normal.en: Impress is the verb, impressive is the adjective, impression is the trace.
normal.cn: impress 是动词，impressive 是形容词，impression 是痕迹。

normal.en: A book impression is one printing run; a wax impression is one pressing.
normal.cn: 一本书的 impression 是一次印次，一块蜡的 impression 是一次压痕。

abstract.en: The word is honest about how opinions form: not reasoned, but pressed in.
abstract.cn: 这个词对看法的形成很诚实：不是推理出来的，而是压进去的。

abstract.en: A single print can outlast the seal that made it, and a first impression can outlast the meeting.
abstract.cn: 一个印痕可能比印章活得更久，一次初印象也可能比那次会面活得更久。

abstract.en: Every imitation is also an impression: it takes the shape of the person being copied.
abstract.cn: 每一种模仿也是一种印样：它取的是被模仿者的形状。

examples.en: She gave the impression of being completely calm.
examples.cn: 她给人一种完全沉着的印象。

examples.en: The impression of her hand stayed in the soft clay.
examples.cn: 她手的压痕留在了软黏土里。

examples.en: I was under the impression that the class had moved.
examples.cn: 我一直以为课已经换了地方。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「印普瑞神」——印上去，气质就神气地留在心里

root: 拉丁语 impressio（压入、印记），来自 imprimere（压入），其词根为 premere（压）；同族词有 impress、impressive、express、compress。

sensesIntro.en: Impression keeps the wax and the mind together: a print, a feeling, a copy and a printing run.
sensesIntro.cn: impression 把蜡与心放在一处：一个印痕、一种感觉、一次模仿、一个印次。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clear print left in wax, matching the seal exactly.
core.cn: 核心意象：蜡上留下的清晰印痕，与印章分毫不差。

branches.en: MIND LINE: the print is left in a person.
branches.cn: 心智线：印痕留在了人身上。

branches.en: SURFACE LINE: the wax or clay keeps the shape.
branches.cn: 表面线：蜡或黏土保留了形状。

branches.en: MIMIC LINE: the print is taken from a living person.
branches.cn: 模仿线：印样取自活人。

branches.en: PRESS LINE: one run of printing is one impression.
branches.cn: 印刷线：一次印刷就是一个印次。

branches.en: CONTRAST: a fact can be checked, an impression only felt.
branches.cn: 对照线：事实可以核实，印象只能感受。

intro.en: The pressing root with an inward prefix and a noun ending that marks result.
intro.cn: 「压」词根配向内前缀与标记结果的名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Imprimere supplies the stem and -io marks the result in Latin.
latinIntro.cn: imprimere 提供词干，拉丁语 -io 标记结果。

items.example: It shows the press going below the surface.
items.exampleCN: 它表示压进了表面之下。

items.example: It is the verb behind the noun.

definition_zh: 令人印象深刻的；令人钦佩的；壮观的
definition_en: so good or large that it makes you admire it
core_image: 一座横跨山谷的桥，走过来的人都不自觉抬头
scene: 考试结束的铃响了，监考老师看了一眼那份写得密密麻麻的答卷。The bridge has an impressive span for a country this size.
sceneCN: 这里 impressive 是「令人印象深刻的」（第 1 个义项：值得赞叹）；句意为对一个这样大小的国家来说，这座桥的跨度令人印象深刻。那座让人抬头的桥，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 形容词：令人印象深刻的；令人钦佩的；壮观的

collocations.zh: 种类丰富得令人惊叹的

derivatives.zh: 去掉 -ive 得到的动词，义为「给……留下印象」
同根名词，义为「印象、印记」
加 -ly 构成，义为「令人印象深刻地」

senses.title: Worthy of admiration
senses.titleCN: 令人钦佩的：值得赞许
senses.definition: causing admiration because of skill or quality
senses.definitionCN: 因技艺或品质而令人赞叹
senses.example: Her handling of the crisis was impressive.
senses.exampleCN: 她对这场危机的处理令人钦佩。
senses.why: The suffix -ive turns the verb into a quality, so impressive describes the thing that does the pressing.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ive 把动词变成性质，因此 impressive 描述的是那个「压」到你的东西。

senses.title: Very large in size
senses.titleCN: 壮观：规模大得使人惊叹
senses.definition: very large or grand, so that it overawes the viewer
senses.definitionCN: 规模或气派大到令人心生敬畏
senses.example: The bridge has an impressive span for a country this size.
senses.exampleCN: 对一个这样大小的国家来说，这座桥的跨度令人印象深刻。
senses.why: Scale works like skill: both leave a mark that the viewer did not expect.
senses.whyCN: 规模与技艺同理：两者都留下观者未曾料到的印痕。

senses.title: Praiseworthy in results
senses.titleCN: 成绩斐然：成效惊人
senses.definition: producing results that command respect
senses.definitionCN: 产生足以赢得尊敬的结果
senses.example: The school showed impressive growth in reading scores.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校的阅读成绩有惊人的提高。
senses.why: Numbers press on the mind as strongly as spectacle, so results also earn the adjective.
senses.whyCN: 数字对心的冲击不亚于奇观，因此成绩也能赢得这个形容词。

senses.title: Striking in appearance
senses.titleCN: 外观出众：一眼看去很有气势
senses.definition: striking to look at, even without deeper quality
senses.definitionCN: 一眼看去很有气势，未必有更深的品质
senses.example: The old station has an impressive front but a shabby hall.
senses.exampleCN: 那座老车站正面很有气势，大厅却很破旧。
senses.why: Appearance can carry the press by itself, which is why the word often appears on tourist signs.
senses.whyCN: 外观本身就能带来冲击，因此这个词常出现在旅游标牌上。

intro.en: Impressive is the adjective formed from impress, with the Latin suffix -ive marking a quality.
intro.cn: impressive 是由 impress 构成的形容词，拉丁词尾 -ive 表示性质。

items.en: Premere, to press, is the root behind the whole family.
items.cn: premere「压」是整个词族背后的词根。

items.en: Imprimere meant to press a mark into something.
items.cn: imprimere 意为「把印痕压进某物」。

items.en: French formed impressif as an adjective of quality.
items.cn: 法语造出 impressif，作为表性质的形容词。

items.en: English adopted it for what compels admiration.
items.cn: 英语采用它，指能赢得赞叹的事物。

items.en: The word then widened from quality to size and spectacle.
items.cn: 此后这个词又从品质扩展到规模与奇观。

note.en: The look-alike group is the impress- adjective family; the near-meaning group holds words of praise.
note.cn: 形近组是 impress- 形容词族；近义组收表示赞许的形容词。

entries.definition: The verb the adjective comes from.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，形容词由它而来。

entries.definition: The mark or feeling that is left.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「印象、印记」。

entries.definition: Describes the person who feels admiration.
entries.definitionCN: 过去分词，描述产生敬佩的那个人。

entries.definition: The adverb of the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词的副词形式。

entries.definition: Very noticeable; close, with less admiration implied.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「显著的」，赞叹意味较轻。

entries.definition: Worth noticing for an unusual quality.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「卓越的」，因不寻常而值得注意。

entries.definition: Visually thrilling; strongest for size and show.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「壮观的」，在规模与场面上最强。

entries.definition: Nothing special; the plain opposite of impressive.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「普通的」，是直接反义。

normalIntro.en: The hooks work on the -ive suffix pair and on the common praise collocations.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子围绕 -ive 后缀的搭配以及常见的赞美搭配。

normal.en: Impressive ends in -ive and describes the cause, not the viewer.
normal.cn: impressive 以 -ive 结尾，描述原因而非观者。

normal.en: Impress the judges, and the result is impressive.
normal.cn: impress the judges，结果就是 impressive。

normal.en: The increase from impressive to more impressive needs the word more.
normal.cn: impressive 的比较级要靠 more。

normal.en: Impressive results is the phrase on every school report.
normal.cn: impressive results 是每份学校报告上的词。

normal.en: The same bridge is impressive up close and pale in photographs.
normal.cn: 同一座桥近看壮观，照片里却暗淡。

abstract.en: Something impressive pressed a mark on you, so the adjective names the pressing force.
abstract.cn: 令人印象深刻之物在你身上留下了印，因此这个形容词命名的是那股压力。

abstract.en: Scale and skill both earn the word, which is why a cliff and a good teacher can share one label.
abstract.cn: 规模与技艺都能赢得这个词，因此一道悬崖和一位好老师能共用一个名号。

abstract.en: Admiration is a print on the mind, and this adjective is the seal that makes it.
abstract.cn: 赞叹是心上的一个印，这个形容词就是压出它的那枚印章。

examples.en: The team made an impressive recovery after the second half.
examples.cn: 下半场之后，球队实现了令人印象深刻的反击。

examples.en: For its price, the phone has an impressive camera.
examples.cn: 就这个价格而言，这款手机的相机令人印象深刻。

examples.en: The hall looks impressive from the outside only.
examples.cn: 这座大厅只是从外面看才显得气势不凡。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「印普瑞西武」——印上去就普瑞（漂亮）、西武（显得威武）

root: 由 impress（拉丁语 imprimere＝in- + premere「压」）加表性质的形容词词尾 -ive 构成；同族词有 impression、impress、impressively、express。

sensesIntro.en: Impressive praises what presses on the mind, whether by skill, size, results or mere appearance.
sensesIntro.cn: impressive 赞许压到心上的东西，无论是技艺、规模、成绩，还是仅有外观。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bridge across a valley that makes every walker look up.
core.cn: 核心意象：横跨山谷的桥，让每个走过的人都抬头。

branches.en: SKILL LINE: the quality of the doing earns praise.
branches.cn: 技艺线：做事的品质赢得赞许。

branches.en: SCALE LINE: size and appearance press on the eye.
branches.cn: 规模线：体量与外观压到眼睛上。

branches.en: RESULT LINE: the numbers themselves command respect.
branches.cn: 成绩线：数字本身就赢得尊敬。

branches.en: AUDIENCE LINE: the adjective assumes someone was moved.
branches.cn: 观众线：这个形容词预设有人被打动。

branches.en: CONTRAST: impressive can be only a surface, remarkable is always real.
branches.cn: 对照线：impressive 可能只是表面，remarkable 总是实在的。

intro.en: The pressing root, an inward prefix, and an adjective suffix that marks a quality worth having.
intro.cn: 「压」词根配向内前缀，再加标记「值得拥有之性质」的形容词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Imprimere supplies the stem and -ive marks the quality in Latin adjectives.
latinIntro.cn: imprimere 提供词干，拉丁形容词词尾 -ive 标记性质。
